RAII helper that starts a timer on construction and stops it on destruction using an rcContext.
Configuration parameters controlling the Recast build process: grid size, cell size/height, agent walkability constraints, and meshing/detail settings.
Linked-list node representing a vertical solid span in a heightfield column with bitfield-compressed min/max and area id.
Fixed-size pool allocator chunk for rcSpan instances used by rcHeightfield to reduce allocation overhead.
Dynamic voxel heightfield representing obstructed space. Stores per-column linked lists of rcSpan with an internal span pool and free list.
Compact cell header holding start index and count of compact spans for a grid column in rcCompactHeightfield.
Compact representation of an open-space span with base y, height, region id, and packed 4-direction neighbor connectivity.
Compact, static heightfield of walkable space derived from rcHeightfield. Stores per-cell compact spans, area ids, and distance/region data.
Represents one layer of a layered heightfield: bounds, raster dimensions, usable extents, and per-cell height/area/connectivity bytes.
Container for multiple rcHeightfieldLayer instances produced when building heightfield layers from a compact heightfield.
Single simple contour: simplified and raw vertex arrays with per-contour region and area ids.
Collection of non-overlapping contours extracted from a compact heightfield's regions, with build-time metadata and bounds.
Polygon mesh suitable for navmesh building: stores vertices, polygon indices with neighbors, per-poly region/flags/area, and bounds/grid info.
Per-polygon detailed mesh data: submesh descriptors, fine vertices, and triangles used to add height/detail to rcPolyMesh polygons.
Bit flags controlling contour simplification and tessellation behavior during rcBuildContours.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int dtStatus;
objects.description: Unsigned integer status code type used by Detour to report operation results. Bitflags indicate high-level result (success, failure, in-progress) and detailed error/info bits. Used with helper functions dtStatusSucceed, dtStatusFailed, dtStatusInProgress, and dtStatusDetail to test status values.

objects.definition:
static const unsigned int DT_FAILURE = 1u << 31;            // Operation failed.
static const unsigned int DT_SUCCESS = 1u << 30;            // Operation succeed.
static const unsigned int DT_IN_PROGRESS = 1u << 29;        // Operation still in progress.

static const unsigned int DT_STATUS_DETAIL_MASK = 0x0ffffff;
static const unsigned int DT_WRONG_MAGIC = 1 << 0;        // Input data is not recognized.
static const unsigned int DT_WRONG_VERSION = 1 << 1;    // Input data is in wrong version.
static const unsigned int DT_OUT_OF_MEMORY = 1 << 2;    // Operation ran out of memory.
static const unsigned int DT_INVALID_PARAM = 1 << 3;    // An input parameter was invalid.
static const unsigned int DT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL = 1 << 4;    // Result buffer for the query was too small to store all results.
static const unsigned int DT_OUT_OF_NODES = 1 << 5;        // Query ran out of nodes during search.
static const unsigned int DT_PARTIAL_RESULT = 1 << 6;    // Query did not reach the end location, returning best guess. 
static const unsigned int DT_ALREADY_OCCUPIED = 1 << 7;    // A tile has already been assigned to the given x,y coordinate
objects.description: Bitmask constants used with dtStatus to encode high-level and detailed operation results. These are values, not types; included here only to document their association with dtStatus. No construction or ownership semantics apply.
Enumeration of node-state flags used during pathfinding. Values indicate whether a node is in the open set, closed set, or if its parent link is detached (came from a raycast).

objects.definition: typedef unsigned short dtNodeIndex;
objects.description: Index type used by dtNodePool to reference nodes in internal arrays and hash buckets. 16-bit unsigned range.

Pathfinding node used by Detour. Stores position, incremental and total costs, parent index (bitfield), per-node extra state, status flags, and the polygon reference this node corresponds to. Parent index and state use DT_NODE_PARENT_BITS and DT_NODE_STATE_BITS, supporting up to DT_MAX_STATES_PER_NODE states per polyRef.

Fixed-capacity pool and hash for allocating, indexing, and querying dtNode instances keyed by dtPolyRef and state. Provides O(1)-ish access via hashed buckets and exposes array index helpers. Copying is disabled; lifetime managed by user via constructor/destructor and clear().

Binary-heap priority queue of dtNode pointers used for the A* open set. Supports push, pop, top, modify (decrease-key-like), and capacity/memory queries. Copying is disabled; user allocates with given capacity n and manages lifetime.

Opaque handle type that uniquely identifies a polygon within a dtNavMesh tile set. Width is 32-bit by default, optionally 64-bit when DT_POLYREF64 is defined. Encodes salt, tile index, and polygon index for validity tracking. Becomes invalid if the owning tile reference changes. Size and bit layout depend on build configuration.

Opaque handle type that uniquely identifies a tile in a dtNavMesh. Width is 32-bit by default, 64-bit with DT_POLYREF64. Invalidated when the tile is removed or the navmesh is reinitialized with different dtNavMeshParams. May be preserved/restored when re-adding the same tile with the same parameters and lastRef.
Bitfield flags that describe ownership/behavior of tile memory blocks stored in a dtMeshTile. Currently defines DT_TILE_FREE_DATA indicating the navmesh owns and frees tile data.
Bitflags returned per-vertex by dtNavMeshQuery::findStraightPath describing special straight-path vertices (start, end, off-mesh connection).
Option flags controlling how dtNavMeshQuery::findStraightPath emits vertices (at area crossings or all crossings).
Option flags for sliced pathfinding that enable any-angle shortcutting using raycasts during search.
Option flags for dtNavMeshQuery::raycast to request cost accumulation along the ray.
Bitflags that mark properties of edges in a detail triangle; currently indicates boundary edges.
Enumerates the type of a polygon in the navmesh: regular ground polygon or an off-mesh connection stub.

Represents a convex polygon within a dtMeshTile: indices into the tile's vertex array, neighbor/linkage info, user flags, vertex count, and packed area/type. Edges/neighbors encoded in neis; firstLink indexes dtLink list within the tile.
Locates and sizes a polygon's associated detail submesh within a tile's detail vertex/triangle arrays.

Internal linked-list node describing adjacency from a polygon edge to a neighbor polygon (possibly in another tile). Stores neighbor ref, owning edge index, side, and sub-edge bounds. Rarely used directly by end users.
Quantized AABB tree node used for tile-level spatial queries over detail geometry. Leaf nodes have non-negative i; negative values encode escape sequences for traversal.
Represents a user-defined traversal connection between two endpoints (A,B) with optional radius, associated polygon index in the tile, link flags, portal side, and a user id.

Metadata header stored at the start of a tile's data describing counts, grid location, agent constraints, bounds, and BV quantization factor. Used during load and by queries to interpret arrays in dtMeshTile.

Holds all per-tile navmesh data: header, base polygons, vertices, links, detail mesh, BV tree, off-mesh connections, raw data buffer, flags, and linkage in free/spatial lists. salt increments on modifications for ref validation. Some pointers may be null depending on content.
Initialization parameters for a dtNavMesh that define grid origin, tile dimensions, and maxima used to size internal tables and reference bit partitions.

Tiled navigation mesh container that owns and indexes dtMeshTile instances, provides add/remove tile management, polygon/tile reference encoding/decoding, and high-level query helpers and state operations. Must be initialized via init() with dtNavMeshParams or single-tile data.
direct_api_constructors: dtNavMesh::init(unsigned char*, const int, const int)

objects.definition: dtNavMesh* dtAllocNavMesh();
objects.description: Factory function allocating a dtNavMesh using Detour's allocator. Returns an uninitialized navmesh which must be initialized via dtNavMesh::init. Caller must free with dtFreeNavMesh.

objects.definition: void dtFreeNavMesh(dtNavMesh* navmesh);
objects.description: Deallocator for dtNavMesh objects created by dtAllocNavMesh. After calling, the pointer becomes invalid.

Holds all input parameters and mesh references required to build a single Detour navmesh tile. It includes base polygon mesh data, optional detail mesh data, optional off-mesh connections, tile indexing/bounds, and agent/grid settings. Used with dtCreateNavMeshData to generate serialized tile data. Many members are pointers to externally owned arrays; the struct does not manage memory.

Polygon traversal filter used by navmesh queries. Holds per-area traversal costs and include/exclude flags and provides passFilter and cost callbacks. It may be compiled with virtual overrides if DT_VIRTUAL_QUERYFILTER is defined; otherwise methods are non-virtual inline for performance.
Output container for dtNavMeshQuery::raycast results: hit parameter and normal, final edge index, optional visited path array with count and capacity, and accumulated path cost.
Abstract callback interface for batched polygon processing used by dtNavMeshQuery::queryPolygons overload. Users derive and implement process().

Main query object for performing pathfinding and local spatial queries against a dtNavMesh. Manages internal node pools and sliced query state and exposes a rich set of operations (findPath, raycast, random point search, etc.). Not copyable.

Alias entry for the factory/free functions is not needed; the class definition above is canonical. Note: construction typically via dtAllocNavMeshQuery() followed by init(). Destruction via dtFreeNavMeshQuery() or delete if allocated otherwise. Missing additional lifecycle details in this header.

objects.definition: dtNavMeshQuery* dtAllocNavMeshQuery();
objects.description: Factory function declaration that allocates a dtNavMeshQuery via Detour allocator. Not a type definition; included here only to note constructor function per instructions.

objects.definition: void dtFreeNavMeshQuery(dtNavMeshQuery* query);
objects.description: Destructor-like API for dtNavMeshQuery allocated with dtAllocNavMeshQuery. Not a type; included only to show lifecycle function.
Header describing a compressed tile cache layer: versioning, tile coordinates, bounds, height range, raster dimensions, and usable subregion extents.
Represents a single rasterized tile layer in the tile cache, including header metadata and per-cell arrays for heights, area IDs, connectivity, regions, and region count.
A single contour extracted from a tile cache layer region. Stores vertex count and packed vertex array, plus region and area identifiers.
A collection of contours generated from a tile cache layer's regions.
A compact polygon mesh built from contours. Stores vertex and polygon counts; arrays for vertices, polygon indices (with fixed verts-per-poly capacity), per-polygon flags, and area IDs.
Abstract allocation interface used by tile cache utilities. Provides reset, alloc, and free hooks; default implementation forwards to dtAlloc/dtFree with DT_ALLOC_TEMP.
Abstract compression interface for tile cache layers. Implementations must provide maxCompressedSize, compress, and decompress for raw/compressed buffers.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int dtObstacleRef;
objects.description: Opaque obstacle reference/handle used by dtTileCache APIs to refer to an obstacle instance. Value packs index and salt bits for validation.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int dtCompressedTileRef;
objects.description: Opaque reference/handle for a compressed tile stored by dtTileCache. Encodes tile index and salt for validation.
Flags controlling ownership/behavior when adding a compressed tile to the cache. Currently indicates whether the navmesh owns and should free the provided tile memory.
Node representing a compressed tile stored in the tile cache, including pointers to compressed payload and raw data, size fields, flags, and freelist linkage. Salt is used for handle validation.
Lifecycle states for an obstacle managed by the tile cache: empty slot, being processed into tiles, processed, or pending removal.
Enumerates supported obstacle geometry types: cylinder, axis-aligned box, and Y-rotated oriented box.
Cylindrical obstacle definition with world-space center position, radius, and height.
Axis-aligned bounding box obstacle defined by min and max corners.
Y-rotated oriented box obstacle. Stores center, half-extents, and a 2-float auxiliary rotation representation derived from half-angle trig terms.

Represents an obstacle tracked by the tile cache, storing its geometric payload (via union), bookkeeping of tiles it touches and those pending rebuild, lifecycle/state fields, salt for handle validation, and freelist linkage.
Configuration parameters for a tile cache, including grid origin and cell size/height, tile dimensions, walkability thresholds, simplification error, and capacity limits for tiles and obstacles.
Customization hook interface allowing a client to post-process polygons (areas/flags) while building navmesh tiles from cached layers.

Primary manager owning compressed tiles and obstacles, handling add/remove of tiles and obstacles, updating/rebuilding affected tiles, and interfacing with a dtNavMesh. Provides encode/decode utilities for handles and maintains freelists and lookups.

A spatial hash/proximity grid used to insert axis-aligned items by ID and query overlapping IDs within a 2D region. The grid partitions space into fixed-size cells (cellSize). Items are stored in an internal pool (Item nodes with id, cell coordinates, and next for chaining) and buckets addressing lists per cell. Bounds track the occupied grid extents. Copy is disabled. Use init to allocate internal storage, addItem to insert by AABB, and queryItems to retrieve overlapping IDs. clear resets contents. getItemCountAt returns number of items in a given grid cell. Note: Only declarations are provided; implementation details such as allocation strategy and bounds semantics are inferred from members. Construction/destruction via dtAllocProximityGrid/dtFreeProximityGrid is supported.

A small utility class that tracks a local obstacle boundary around a point on a Detour navmesh. It stores up to 8 nearby boundary segments (each as two 3D points, packed into a 6-float array) and up to 16 recent polygons around a center. It can be updated from a navmesh query and filtered, validated against the navmesh, and queried for the center and segments. Copying is disabled. Construction/destruction are default; ownership/lifetime is by user code.
Represents a circular obstacle used by the obstacle avoidance system, including position, current and desired velocity, radius, and helper vectors for sampling-side selection.
Represents a static line-segment obstacle with endpoints p and q and a flag indicating if the agent is touching or near the segment.

Holds per-sample debugging information for obstacle avoidance velocity sampling, including velocities, sizes, and various penalty components. Construction is via dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceDebugData and destruction via dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceDebugData. Non-copyable.

Tunable parameters for obstacle avoidance sampling, including velocity bias, weighting factors, time horizon, and grid/adaptive sampling configuration. Values are consumed by dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery sampling methods.

Main query object that collects obstacle primitives and computes collision-free velocities using grid or adaptive sampling. Must be initialized with capacity, then obstacles added via addCircle/addSegment. Sampling methods output chosen velocity and optionally log debug samples. Non-copyable. Allocate with dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceQuery and release with dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceQuery.

A dynamic path corridor used by Detour to represent, maintain, and locally optimize an agent's navigation path across a navmesh. Holds start/target positions and an array of dtPolyRef path polygons. Provides methods for initialization, resetting to a position, generating straight-path corners, topology/visibility optimization, validating/trimming the path, moving agent/target positions, and loading a path. Construction is via default ctor then init(maxPath). Copying is disabled; manage via pointers or value with care.

objects.definition: typedef unsigned int dtPathQueueRef;
objects.description: Opaque handle type used to identify a queued path request within dtPathQueue. It is an unsigned integer reference value; DT_PATHQ_INVALID (0) denotes an invalid handle.

Queue manager for asynchronous or batched pathfinding requests over a Detour navigation mesh. It maintains a small fixed-size queue (MAX_QUEUE=8) of pending path queries and processes them via an internal dtNavMeshQuery. Clients call request(...) to enqueue a pathfind described by start/end refs and positions with an optional filter, then poll getRequestStatus(...) and retrieve results via getPathResult(...). Lifetime: construct, call init(...) to bind a dtNavMesh and configure buffer sizes, periodically call update(...) to advance work, and destroy to release internal resources. Copying is disabled. Note: PathQuery is a private internal struct; details and memory ownership of path buffers are managed inside dtPathQueue.
Enumeration of primitive types supported by the debug draw interface: points, lines, triangles, and quads.

Abstract interface for debug rendering backends. Provides methods to control depth mask, textures, begin/end drawing with a primitive type and size, submit vertices (with optional UVs), and map an area id to a color. Destructor is pure virtual, indicating abstract base. Implementations must provide rendering details.

Concrete debug draw that records submitted geometry into an internal display list (positions and colors) for later playback via draw(). Manages capacity-resizing, primitive type, size, and depth mask state. Copying is disabled. Ownership and lifetime of internal buffers handled internally.
Opaque forward-declared handle to a debug drawing interface used by the Recast debug draw helpers. Only referenced here; no definition provided in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast heightfield type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast compact heightfield type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast heightfield layer type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast heightfield layer set type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast contour set type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast polygon mesh type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.
Opaque forward-declared Recast detailed polygon mesh type referenced by the debug draw helpers. Not defined in this header.

Bitmask flags controlling what elements are drawn by the Detour debug drawing helpers (off-mesh connections, closed list nodes, and tile coloring). Intended for use with the duDebugDrawNavMesh* functions. Values can be ORed together.

Abstract I/O interface used by the dump/read utilities. Provides virtual methods to determine direction (writing/reading) and to read/write raw bytes. The destructor is virtual and declared but not defined here. Concrete implementations are expected to handle persistence to files, memory, etc.

functions.name: rcAssertFailSetCustom
functions.signature: void rcAssertFailSetCustom(rcAssertFailFunc* assertFailFunc);
functions.description: Registers the base custom assertion-failure callback used by Recast’s rcAssert macro. When non-null, the callback is invoked on a failed rcAssert with the stringified expression, source file, and line. When null, rcAssert falls back to the standard C assert(). Use this to install or clear a global assertion handler.
requirements: assertFailFunc may be NULL to clear the custom handler and revert to standard assert() behavior.
If non-NULL, assertFailFunc must have the signature: void(const char* expression, const char* file, int line).

The installed callback should be prepared to be called whenever an rcAssert fails and must not assume any particular program state. Other behavioral guarantees (e.g., termination, logging) are not specified in this header.
Thread-safety and lifetime management of the provided function pointer are unspecified in this header (unknown).

functions.name: rcAssertFailGetCustom
functions.signature: rcAssertFailFunc* rcAssertFailGetCustom();
functions.description: Returns the current base custom assertion-failure callback used by rcAssert, or NULL if no custom handler is set and the default C assert() will be used.
requirements: No arguments required.
Return value may be NULL if no custom handler is installed.
The caller must not assume any threading or ownership semantics from the returned pointer; only use it as a callable function pointer if non-NULL (other details unknown).

functions.name: rcAllocSetCustom
functions.signature: void rcAllocSetCustom(rcAllocFunc* allocFunc, rcFreeFunc* freeFunc);
functions.description: Sets the global custom allocation and deallocation callbacks used by Recast’s rcAlloc/rcFree. Call this early in program startup to route Recast allocations through your allocator.
requirements: allocFunc must be a valid function pointer of type rcAllocFunc (void* f(size_t, rcAllocHint)).
freeFunc must be a valid function pointer of type rcFreeFunc (void f(void*)).
Must be called before calling rcAlloc/rcFree to affect their behavior; calling after allocations have already occurred will not retroactively change how prior memory must be freed.

functions.name: rcAlloc
functions.signature: void* rcAlloc(size_t size, rcAllocHint hint);
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of the given size, using either the default allocator or the custom one set via rcAllocSetCustom. The hint indicates expected lifetime (temporary vs. permanent) to help the allocator choose a pool/strategy.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; may be 0 but will likely return NULL.
hint must be a valid rcAllocHint (RC_ALLOC_PERM or RC_ALLOC_TEMP).
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL before use.
Memory must be released with rcFree(void*). Do not free with delete/delete[]/free().

functions.name: rcFree
functions.signature: void rcFree(void* ptr);
functions.description: Deallocates a memory block previously returned by rcAlloc (or by the custom rcAllocFunc). Passing NULL is a no-op. Note: it does not null out the caller’s pointer.
requirements: ptr must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by rcAlloc (or the custom rcAllocFunc) and not already freed.
After rcFree(ptr) returns, the memory is invalid; do not dereference ptr unless you reset it yourself.
Do not mix allocation/deallocation APIs (i.e., do not pass memory from new/malloc to rcFree).

functions.name: operator new
functions.signature: inline void* operator new(size_t, const rcNewTag&, void* p);
functions.description: Placement-style new used internally to construct an object at a pre-allocated address, disambiguated by rcNewTag to avoid clashing with the STL placement new. Returns the provided address unmodified.
requirements: p must point to a valid, suitably aligned memory region large enough to hold the object being constructed.
The lifetime and deallocation of memory pointed to by p are managed by the caller; this operator does not allocate memory.
rcNewTag must be passed to select this overload.

functions.name: operator delete
functions.signature: inline void operator delete(void*, const rcNewTag&, void*);
functions.description: Matching placement delete for the rcNewTag placement new. Does nothing; present only for exception-safety/matching lookup requirements.
requirements: Only used by the compiler if a constructor throws during placement new with rcNewTag; it performs no action.
The memory pointed to is not released by this operator; caller must manage it.

functions.name: rcTempVector::rcTempVector
functions.signature: rcTempVector();
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty temporary-lifetime vector (storage allocated using RC_ALLOC_TEMP via rcAlloc).
requirements: No preconditions. Initially size()==0 and capacity()==0.

functions.name: rcTempVector::rcTempVector
functions.signature: explicit rcTempVector(rcSizeType size);
functions.description: Constructs a temporary-lifetime vector with size elements value-initialized (default-constructed).
requirements: T must be default-constructible.
size must be >= 0 and not exceed RC_SIZE_MAX.
Allocation may fail internally; if it does, the vector remains empty.

functions.name: rcTempVector::rcTempVector
functions.signature: rcTempVector(rcSizeType size, const T& value);
functions.description: Constructs a temporary-lifetime vector with size elements, each copy-constructed from value.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
size must be >= 0 and not exceed RC_SIZE_MAX.
value must remain valid during construction (until the constructor completes).

functions.name: rcTempVector::rcTempVector
functions.signature: rcTempVector(const rcTempVector<T>& other);
functions.description: Copy-constructs a temporary-lifetime vector from another rcTempVector, copying all elements.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
other.begin()..other.end() must be a valid range.

functions.name: rcPermVector::rcPermVector
functions.signature: rcPermVector();
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty permanent-lifetime vector (storage allocated using RC_ALLOC_PERM via rcAlloc).
requirements: No preconditions. Initially size()==0 and capacity()==0.

functions.name: rcPermVector::rcPermVector
functions.signature: explicit rcPermVector(rcSizeType size);
functions.description: Constructs a permanent-lifetime vector with size elements value-initialized (default-constructed).
requirements: T must be default-constructible.
size must be >= 0 and not exceed RC_SIZE_MAX.
Allocation may fail internally; if it does, the vector remains empty.

functions.name: rcPermVector::rcPermVector
functions.signature: rcPermVector(rcSizeType size, const T& value);
functions.description: Constructs a permanent-lifetime vector with size elements, each copy-constructed from value.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
size must be >= 0 and not exceed RC_SIZE_MAX.
value must remain valid during construction (until the constructor completes).

functions.name: rcPermVector::rcPermVector
functions.signature: rcPermVector(const rcPermVector<T>& other);
functions.description: Copy-constructs a permanent-lifetime vector from another rcPermVector, copying all elements.
requirements: T must be copy-constructible.
other.begin()..other.end() must be a valid range.

functions.name: rcScopedDelete::rcScopedDelete
functions.signature: inline rcScopedDelete();
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty scoped deleter that manages no pointer. On destruction, does nothing.
requirements: No preconditions.

functions.name: rcScopedDelete::rcScopedDelete
functions.signature: inline rcScopedDelete(T* p);
functions.description: Constructs a scoped deleter that will free the provided pointer with rcFree when the deleter is destroyed. Intended for arrays or buffers allocated via rcAlloc.
requirements: p must be either NULL or a pointer obtained from rcAlloc (or a compatible rcAllocFunc); memory must be safe to free with rcFree.
Ownership is non-copyable; rcScopedDelete is not copyable (copy constructor and assignment are disabled).

functions.name: rcScopedDelete::~rcScopedDelete
functions.signature: inline ~rcScopedDelete();
functions.description: Destructor that calls rcFree(ptr) on the managed pointer, if any.
requirements: The managed pointer must be valid to pass to rcFree (or NULL).
Caller must not have already freed the pointer via other means.

functions.name: rcScopedDelete::operator T*
functions.signature: inline operator T*();
functions.description: Implicit conversion to the managed raw pointer. Useful to pass to APIs expecting T*. Does not release ownership.
requirements: May return NULL if no pointer is managed.
Use with care; this does not transfer ownership or inhibit the destructor from freeing the pointer.

functions.name: rcIgnoreUnused
functions.signature: template<class T> void rcIgnoreUnused(const T&)
functions.description: Helper template that accepts any parameter and does nothing, used to silence unused-parameter warnings.
requirements: No requirements; pass any value or reference of any type.

functions.name: rcContext::enableLog
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::enableLog(bool state)
functions.description: Enables or disables logging on the rcContext instance.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
When disabled, subsequent log() calls have no effect.

functions.name: rcContext::resetLog
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::resetLog()

Has effect only if logging is enabled via enableLog(true).

functions.name: rcContext::log
functions.signature: void rcContext::log(const rcLogCategory category, const char* format, ...)
functions.description: Logs a formatted message under the given category. Concrete rcContext implementations should override doLog to handle the message.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
format must be a valid printf-style C string; variadic arguments must match the format.
If logging is disabled, the call may be ignored.

functions.name: rcContext::enableTimer
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::enableTimer(bool state)
functions.description: Enables or disables performance timers on the rcContext instance.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
When disabled, timer operations have no effect and getAccumulatedTime returns -1.

functions.name: rcContext::resetTimers
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::resetTimers()
functions.description: Resets all timers to unused if timers are enabled (calls doResetTimers).
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
Has effect only if timers are enabled via enableTimer(true).

functions.name: rcContext::startTimer
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::startTimer(const rcTimerLabel label)
functions.description: Starts the specified performance timer if timers are enabled.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
label must be a valid rcTimerLabel value.
Has effect only if timers are enabled.

functions.name: rcContext::stopTimer
functions.signature: inline void rcContext::stopTimer(const rcTimerLabel label)
functions.description: Stops the specified performance timer if timers are enabled.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
label must be a valid rcTimerLabel value.
Has effect only if timers are enabled.

functions.name: rcContext::getAccumulatedTime
functions.signature: inline int rcContext::getAccumulatedTime(const rcTimerLabel label) const
functions.description: Returns the total accumulated time for the given timer label, or -1 if timers are disabled or the timer has never been started.
requirements: The rcContext instance must be valid.
label must be a valid rcTimerLabel value.

functions.name: rcScopedTimer::rcScopedTimer
functions.signature: inline rcScopedTimer::rcScopedTimer(rcContext* ctx, const rcTimerLabel label)
functions.description: RAII helper that starts the given timer on construction and will stop it in the destructor when going out of scope.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null rcContext pointer.
label must be a valid rcTimerLabel value.
Timers should be enabled on ctx for effects to be recorded.

functions.name: rcCalcBounds
functions.signature: void rcCalcBounds(const float* verts, int numVerts, float* minBounds, float* maxBounds)
functions.description: Computes axis-aligned bounding box (min/max) for an array of 3D vertices.
requirements: verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats.
numVerts must be >= 0; if 0, behavior is implementation-defined/unknown.
minBounds and maxBounds must each be valid float[3] output buffers.

functions.name: rcCalcGridSize
functions.signature: void rcCalcGridSize(const float* minBounds, const float* maxBounds, float cellSize, int* sizeX, int* sizeZ)
functions.description: Calculates grid width and height in cells for an AABB and xz-plane cell size.
requirements: minBounds and maxBounds must each be valid float[3] inputs.
cellSize must be > 0.
sizeX and sizeZ must be valid output pointers.

functions.name: rcCreateHeightfield
functions.signature: bool rcCreateHeightfield(rcContext* context, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int sizeX, int sizeZ, const float* minBounds, const float* maxBounds, float cellSize, float cellHeight)
functions.description: Initializes an allocated rcHeightfield with dimensions, bounds, and cell sizing.
requirements: context may be null only if caller ignores logging; otherwise must be valid.
heightfield must be allocated and uninitialized/ready for init.
sizeX and sizeZ must be >= 0.
minBounds and maxBounds must be valid float[3] pointers.
cellSize > 0 and cellHeight > 0.
Returns true on success; false on allocation/initialization failure.

functions.name: rcMarkWalkableTriangles
functions.signature: void rcMarkWalkableTriangles(rcContext* context, float walkableSlopeAngle, const float* verts, int numVerts, const int* tris, int numTris, unsigned char* triAreaIDs)
functions.description: Marks triangles with slope below walkableSlopeAngle as RC_WALKABLE_AREA; leaves others unchanged.
requirements: walkableSlopeAngle must satisfy 0 <= value < 90 (degrees).
verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats.
tris must point to at least 3*numTris ints indexing verts.
triAreaIDs must be an array of length >= numTris for output.
context optional for logging.

functions.name: rcClearUnwalkableTriangles
functions.signature: void rcClearUnwalkableTriangles(rcContext* context, float walkableSlopeAngle, const float* verts, int numVerts, const int* tris, int numTris, unsigned char* triAreaIDs)
functions.description: Marks triangles with slope >= walkableSlopeAngle as RC_NULL_AREA; leaves others unchanged.
requirements: walkableSlopeAngle must satisfy 0 <= value < 90 (degrees).
verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats.
tris must point to at least 3*numTris ints indexing verts.
triAreaIDs must be an array of length >= numTris for output.
context optional for logging.

functions.name: rcAddSpan
functions.signature: bool rcAddSpan(rcContext* context, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int x, int z, unsigned short spanMin, unsigned short spanMax, unsigned char areaID, int flagMergeThreshold)
functions.description: Adds a span to the given heightfield column, merging as needed and optionally merging flags when within the merge threshold.
requirements: heightfield must be an initialized rcHeightfield.
0 <= x < heightfield.width; 0 <= z < heightfield.height.
spanMin < spanMax and spanMax <= RC_SPAN_MAX_HEIGHT.
areaID must be <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
flagMergeThreshold >= 0.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcRasterizeTriangle
functions.signature: bool rcRasterizeTriangle(rcContext* context, const float* v0, const float* v1, const float* v2, unsigned char areaID, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int flagMergeThreshold = 1)
functions.description: Rasterizes a single triangle into the heightfield, adding spans where the triangle overlaps the grid.
requirements: heightfield must be initialized.
v0, v1, v2 must each be valid float[3] pointers.
areaID must be <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
flagMergeThreshold >= 0.
Returns true on success; triangles not overlapping grid add no spans.

functions.name: rcRasterizeTriangles
functions.signature: bool rcRasterizeTriangles(rcContext* context, const float* verts, int numVerts, const int* tris, const unsigned char* triAreaIDs, int numTris, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int flagMergeThreshold = 1)
functions.description: Rasterizes an indexed triangle mesh (int indices) into the heightfield.
requirements: heightfield must be initialized.
verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats.
tris must point to at least 3*numTris ints.
triAreaIDs must have length >= numTris; values <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
flagMergeThreshold >= 0.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcRasterizeTriangles
functions.signature: bool rcRasterizeTriangles(rcContext* context, const float* verts, int numVerts, const unsigned short* tris, const unsigned char* triAreaIDs, int numTris, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int flagMergeThreshold = 1)
functions.description: Rasterizes an indexed triangle mesh (unsigned short indices) into the heightfield.
requirements: heightfield must be initialized.
verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats.
tris must point to at least 3*numTris unsigned shorts.
triAreaIDs must have length >= numTris; values <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
flagMergeThreshold >= 0.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcRasterizeTriangles
functions.signature: bool rcRasterizeTriangles(rcContext* context, const float* verts, const unsigned char* triAreaIDs, int numTris, rcHeightfield& heightfield, int flagMergeThreshold = 1)
functions.description: Rasterizes a triangle list where each triangle is given as 9 sequential floats (3 vertices).
requirements: heightfield must be initialized.
verts must contain at least 9*numTris floats (ax,ay,az,bx,by,bz,cx,cy,cz per tri).
triAreaIDs must have length >= numTris; values <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
flagMergeThreshold >= 0.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcFilterLowHangingWalkableObstacles
functions.signature: void rcFilterLowHangingWalkableObstacles(rcContext* context, int walkableClimb, rcHeightfield& heightfield)
functions.description: Marks obstacle spans as walkable when their top is within walkableClimb of the walkable span below, smoothing small obstacles and steps.
requirements: heightfield must be fully built (all spans added).
walkableClimb >= 0 (in voxels).

functions.name: rcFilterLedgeSpans
functions.signature: void rcFilterLedgeSpans(rcContext* context, int walkableHeight, int walkableClimb, rcHeightfield& heightfield)
functions.description: Marks ledge spans as non-walkable when neighboring span tops differ by more than walkableClimb; helps remove overhang artifacts.
requirements: heightfield must be fully built (all spans added).
walkableHeight >= 3 (voxels).
walkableClimb >= 0 (voxels).

functions.name: rcFilterWalkableLowHeightSpans
functions.signature: void rcFilterWalkableLowHeightSpans(rcContext* context, int walkableHeight, rcHeightfield& heightfield)
functions.description: Marks spans as non-walkable if clearance above them is less than walkableHeight.
requirements: heightfield must be fully built (all spans added).
walkableHeight >= 3 (voxels).

functions.name: rcGetHeightFieldSpanCount
functions.signature: int rcGetHeightFieldSpanCount(rcContext* context, const rcHeightfield& heightfield)
functions.description: Returns the total number of spans contained in the heightfield.
requirements: heightfield must be initialized.

functions.name: rcBuildCompactHeightfield
functions.signature: bool rcBuildCompactHeightfield(rcContext* context, int walkableHeight, int walkableClimb, const rcHeightfield& heightfield, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Builds a compact heightfield of open space from a source heightfield of solid space; first step before distance/region processing.
requirements: heightfield must be valid and fully built.
compactHeightfield must be pre-allocated for output.
walkableHeight >= 3 (voxels).
walkableClimb >= 0 (voxels).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcErodeWalkableArea
functions.signature: bool rcErodeWalkableArea(rcContext* context, int erosionRadius, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Erodes walkable areas by the given radius (in voxels), marking cells near obstructions as un-walkable.
requirements: compactHeightfield must be populated (built).
erosionRadius must satisfy 0 < value < 255.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcMedianFilterWalkableArea
functions.signature: bool rcMedianFilterWalkableArea(rcContext* context, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Applies a median filter to area ids to reduce noise in the compact heightfield.
requirements: compactHeightfield must be populated (built).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcMarkBoxArea
functions.signature: void rcMarkBoxArea(rcContext* context, const float* boxMinBounds, const float* boxMaxBounds, unsigned char areaId, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Applies an area id to all spans whose world-space positions lie within the given axis-aligned bounding box.
requirements: compactHeightfield must be populated (built).
boxMinBounds and boxMaxBounds must be valid float[3] pointers (world units).
areaId <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.

functions.name: rcMarkConvexPolyArea
functions.signature: void rcMarkConvexPolyArea(rcContext* context, const float* verts, int numVerts, float minY, float maxY, unsigned char areaId, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Applies an area id to spans within the projection of a convex polygon extruded between minY and maxY in world units.
requirements: compactHeightfield must be populated (built).
verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats; numVerts is the polygon vertex count.
areaId <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.
minY and maxY are world heights; relationship constraints not explicitly stated, but expected minY <= maxY.

functions.name: rcOffsetPoly
functions.signature: int rcOffsetPoly(const float* verts, int numVerts, float offset, float* outVerts, int maxOutVerts)
functions.description: Offsets a convex polygon outward along vertex normals by offset; bevels sharp corners; writes result to outVerts.
requirements: verts must point to at least 3*numVerts floats representing a convex polygon.
numVerts must be >= 0; function requires sufficient convexity for meaningful results.
outVerts must have capacity for up to 2*numVerts vertices (i.e., at least 3*(2*numVerts) floats).
maxOutVerts must reflect the capacity of outVerts; if insufficient, function returns 0.
Returns the number of output vertices, or 0 on failure/insufficient space.

functions.name: rcMarkCylinderArea
functions.signature: void rcMarkCylinderArea(rcContext* context, const float* position, float radius, float height, unsigned char areaId, rcCompactHeightfield& compactHeightfield)
functions.description: Applies an area id to all spans within a vertical cylinder defined by base center, radius, and height.
requirements: compactHeightfield must be populated (built).
position must be a valid float[3] (world units).
radius > 0 and height > 0 (world units).
areaId <= RC_WALKABLE_AREA.

functions.name: rcBuildDistanceField
functions.signature: bool rcBuildDistanceField(rcContext* ctx, rcCompactHeightfield& chf)
functions.description: Builds the distance-to-boundary field for a populated compact heightfield.
requirements: chf must be a populated compact heightfield.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildRegions
functions.signature: bool rcBuildRegions(rcContext* ctx, rcCompactHeightfield& chf, int borderSize, int minRegionArea, int mergeRegionArea)
functions.description: Builds region assignments using watershed partitioning over the compact heightfield.
requirements: chf must be a populated compact heightfield.
borderSize >= 0 (voxels).
minRegionArea >= 0 (voxels).
mergeRegionArea >= 0 (voxels).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildLayerRegions
functions.signature: bool rcBuildLayerRegions(rcContext* ctx, rcCompactHeightfield& chf, int borderSize, int minRegionArea)
functions.description: Partitions the compact heightfield into non-overlapping layers (region data).
requirements: chf must be a populated compact heightfield.
borderSize >= 0 (voxels).
minRegionArea >= 0 (voxels).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildRegionsMonotone
functions.signature: bool rcBuildRegionsMonotone(rcContext* ctx, rcCompactHeightfield& chf, int borderSize, int minRegionArea, int mergeRegionArea)
functions.description: Builds regions using monotone partitioning, a simpler alternative to watershed.
requirements: chf must be a populated compact heightfield.
borderSize >= 0 (voxels).
minRegionArea >= 0 (voxels).
mergeRegionArea >= 0 (voxels).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcSetCon
functions.signature: inline void rcSetCon(rcCompactSpan& span, int direction, int neighborIndex)
functions.description: Sets the packed neighbor connection index for the given span and direction (0..3).
requirements: direction must satisfy 0 <= direction < 4.
neighborIndex is stored modulo 6 bits (masked with 0x3f).
span must be a valid rcCompactSpan reference.

functions.name: rcGetCon
functions.signature: inline int rcGetCon(const rcCompactSpan& span, int direction)
functions.description: Gets the packed neighbor connection index for the given direction, or RC_NOT_CONNECTED if none.
requirements: direction must satisfy 0 <= direction < 4.
span must be a valid rcCompactSpan reference.

functions.name: rcGetDirOffsetX
functions.signature: inline int rcGetDirOffsetX(int direction)
functions.description: Returns the x-axis cell offset for the given 4-connected direction (0..3).
requirements: direction must be in 0..3 (masked internally).

functions.name: rcGetDirOffsetY
functions.signature: inline int rcGetDirOffsetY(int direction)
functions.description: Returns the z-axis cell offset for the given 4-connected direction (0..3).
requirements: direction must be in 0..3 (masked internally).

functions.name: rcGetDirForOffset
functions.signature: inline int rcGetDirForOffset(int offsetX, int offsetZ)
functions.description: Returns the 4-connected direction code that corresponds to the given unit offset (one of offsetX or offsetZ should be 0).
requirements: offsetX must be in [-1, 1].
offsetZ must be in [-1, 1].
One of offsetX or offsetZ should be 0; diagonal inputs are invalid/undefined.

functions.name: rcBuildHeightfieldLayers
functions.signature: bool rcBuildHeightfieldLayers(rcContext* ctx, const rcCompactHeightfield& chf, int borderSize, int walkableHeight, rcHeightfieldLayerSet& lset)
functions.description: Builds a set of heightfield layers from a fully built compact heightfield.
requirements: chf must be a fully built compact heightfield.
borderSize >= 0 (voxels).
walkableHeight >= 3 (voxels).
lset must be pre-allocated for output.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildContours
functions.signature: bool rcBuildContours(rcContext* ctx, const rcCompactHeightfield& chf, float maxError, int maxEdgeLen, rcContourSet& cset, int buildFlags = RC_CONTOUR_TESS_WALL_EDGES)
functions.description: Extracts and simplifies region outlines into a contour set from a compact heightfield.
requirements: chf must be a fully built compact heightfield with regions.
maxError >= 0 (world units).
maxEdgeLen >= 0 (voxels).
cset must be pre-allocated for output.
buildFlags is a bitmask of rcBuildContoursFlags.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildPolyMesh
functions.signature: bool rcBuildPolyMesh(rcContext* ctx, const rcContourSet& cset, const int nvp, rcPolyMesh& mesh)
functions.description: Builds a polygon mesh from a contour set with up to nvp vertices per polygon.
requirements: cset must be a fully built contour set.
nvp >= 3.
mesh must be pre-allocated for output (empty).
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcMergePolyMeshes
functions.signature: bool rcMergePolyMeshes(rcContext* ctx, rcPolyMesh** meshes, const int nmeshes, rcPolyMesh& mesh)
functions.description: Merges multiple rcPolyMesh meshes into a single rcPolyMesh.
requirements: meshes must point to an array of nmeshes valid rcPolyMesh* pointers.
nmeshes must be >= 1.
mesh must be pre-allocated for output.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcBuildPolyMeshDetail
functions.signature: bool rcBuildPolyMeshDetail(rcContext* ctx, const rcPolyMesh& mesh, const rcCompactHeightfield& chf, float sampleDist, float sampleMaxError, rcPolyMeshDetail& dmesh)
functions.description: Builds a detail mesh that captures height detail over the input polygon mesh using the compact heightfield.
requirements: mesh must be a fully built polygon mesh.
chf must be the compact heightfield used to build the mesh.
sampleDist >= 0 (world units).
sampleMaxError >= 0 (world units).
dmesh must be pre-allocated for output.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcCopyPolyMesh
functions.signature: bool rcCopyPolyMesh(rcContext* ctx, const rcPolyMesh& src, rcPolyMesh& dst)
functions.description: Copies the contents of a polygon mesh from src to an empty dst mesh.
requirements: src must be a valid rcPolyMesh.
dst must be pre-allocated and an empty mesh before copy.
Returns true on success.

functions.name: rcMergePolyMeshDetails
functions.signature: bool rcMergePolyMeshDetails(rcContext* ctx, rcPolyMeshDetail** meshes, const int nmeshes, rcPolyMeshDetail& mesh)
functions.description: Merges multiple rcPolyMeshDetail meshes into a single detail mesh.
requirements: meshes must be an array of nmeshes valid rcPolyMeshDetail* pointers.
nmeshes >= 1.
mesh must be pre-allocated for output.
Returns true on success.

functions.description: Frees a polygon mesh allocated with rcAllocPolyMesh.

Do not free the same pointer more than once.

functions.name: rcSqrt
functions.signature: float rcSqrt(float x)
functions.description: Returns the square root of x.
requirements: Input is a float; domain-specific behavior for negative x is unknown (implementation-defined).

functions.name: rcVcross
functions.signature: inline void rcVcross(float* dest, const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Computes the 3D cross product v1 x v2 and stores it in dest.
requirements: dest must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVdot
functions.signature: inline float rcVdot(const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Computes the 3D dot product v1 · v2.
requirements: v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVmad
functions.signature: inline void rcVmad(float* dest, const float* v1, const float* v2, const float s)
functions.description: Computes dest = v1 + v2*s for 3D vectors.
requirements: dest must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVadd
functions.signature: inline void rcVadd(float* dest, const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Computes dest = v1 + v2 element-wise for 3D vectors.
requirements: dest must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVsub
functions.signature: inline void rcVsub(float* dest, const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Computes dest = v1 - v2 element-wise for 3D vectors.
requirements: dest must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVmin
functions.signature: inline void rcVmin(float* mn, const float* v)
functions.description: Selects per-component minima: mn[i] = min(mn[i], v[i]) for i in {0,1,2}.
requirements: mn must be a valid float[3] buffer containing initial values.
v must be a valid float[3] input.

functions.name: rcVmax
functions.signature: inline void rcVmax(float* mx, const float* v)
functions.description: Selects per-component maxima: mx[i] = max(mx[i], v[i]) for i in {0,1,2}.
requirements: mx must be a valid float[3] buffer containing initial values.
v must be a valid float[3] input.

functions.name: rcVcopy
functions.signature: inline void rcVcopy(float* dest, const float* v)
functions.description: Copies 3D vector v into dest.
requirements: dest must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v must be a valid float[3] input.

functions.name: rcVdist
functions.signature: inline float rcVdist(const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Returns Euclidean distance between two 3D points.
requirements: v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVdistSqr
functions.signature: inline float rcVdistSqr(const float* v1, const float* v2)
functions.description: Returns squared Euclidean distance between two 3D points.
requirements: v1 and v2 must each be valid float[3] inputs.

functions.name: rcVnormalize
functions.signature: inline void rcVnormalize(float* v)
functions.description: Normalizes a 3D vector in place to unit length.
requirements: v must be a valid float[3] buffer.
v must not be the zero vector to avoid division by zero (inferred from algorithm).

functions.name: rcSwap
functions.signature: template<class T> inline void rcSwap(T& a, T& b)
functions.description: Swaps the values of a and b.
requirements: a and b must be valid references to swappable types (copy-constructible/assignable).

functions.name: rcMin
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T rcMin(T a, T b)
functions.description: Returns the minimum of a and b using operator<.
requirements: Type T must define operator< and be copyable.

functions.name: rcMax
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T rcMax(T a, T b)
functions.description: Returns the maximum of a and b using operator>.
requirements: Type T must define operator> and be copyable.

functions.name: rcAbs
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T rcAbs(T a)
functions.description: Returns the absolute value of a using comparison to 0 and unary minus.
requirements: Type T must support comparison to 0 and unary negation; behavior for unsigned types may be trivial.

functions.name: rcSqr
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T rcSqr(T a)
functions.description: Returns the square of a (a*a).
requirements: Type T must support multiplication and be copyable.

functions.name: rcClamp
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T rcClamp(T value, T minInclusive, T maxInclusive)
functions.description: Clamps value to the inclusive range [minInclusive, maxInclusive].
requirements: Type T must support comparisons (<, >).
Caller should ensure minInclusive <= maxInclusive for meaningful results.

functions.name: dtAssertFailSetCustom
functions.signature: void dtAssertFailSetCustom(dtAssertFailFunc* assertFailFunc);
functions.description: Registers a custom assertion failure callback for Detour assertions. When set, dtAssert will invoke this callback instead of the standard assert when an assertion fails. If a null pointer is provided (or no custom function is set), dtAssert falls back to the C library assert. Only available when RC_DISABLE_ASSERTS is not defined at compile time.
requirements: Only available if the header is compiled without RC_DISABLE_ASSERTS defined.
The assertFailFunc argument must be either NULL or a valid function pointer matching typedef: void(const char* expression, const char* file, int line).
If a non-NULL function pointer is provided, the function must remain valid for as long as dtAssert may call it (e.g., until replaced or program end).
The custom failure function should not assume expression, file, or line are non-null-terminated beyond standard C strings; they are provided as const char* and an int line number.

requirements: Only available if the header is compiled without RC_DISABLE_ASSERTS defined.
Callers must handle a NULL return value, which indicates that dtAssert will use the standard assert.

functions.name: dtAllocSetCustom
functions.signature: void dtAllocSetCustom(dtAllocFunc* allocFunc, dtFreeFunc* freeFunc);
functions.description: Registers custom allocation and deallocation functions to be used by the Detour allocator (dtAlloc/dtFree). Use this to plug in your own memory management. Typically called during initialization before any allocations that should use the custom hooks. Unknowns: whether passing null resets to defaults or is allowed; thread-safety and lifetime of the function pointers are not documented.
requirements: allocFunc must be a function matching typedef: void* (dtAllocFunc)(size_t size, dtAllocHint hint). It should return a valid pointer on success or null on failure.
freeFunc must be a function matching typedef: void (dtFreeFunc)(void* ptr). It should accept pointers previously returned by the corresponding allocator.
If you intend all subsequent allocations to use the custom functions, call this before any calls to dtAlloc/dtFree that should be affected.
The provided function pointers must remain valid for as long as they may be invoked by the library (lifetime not documented; ensure they outlive their use).
Behavior when passing null for either function pointer is unknown.

functions.name: dtAlloc
functions.signature: void* dtAlloc(size_t size, dtAllocHint hint);
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of the requested size using the Detour allocator, optionally guided by a usage-lifetime hint (DT_ALLOC_PERM or DT_ALLOC_TEMP). Returns a pointer to the beginning of the block or null on allocation failure. Use dtFree to release the memory.
requirements: size is the number of bytes to allocate; no minimum/maximum documented.
hint must be a valid dtAllocHint value (DT_ALLOC_PERM or DT_ALLOC_TEMP).
Caller must check the return value for null before dereferencing or using the memory.
Memory obtained from dtAlloc must be released by calling dtFree with the same pointer when no longer needed.
Alignment, zero-initialization, and error-reporting details are not documented (assume unspecified).

functions.name: dtFree
functions.signature: void dtFree(void* ptr);
functions.description: Deallocates a memory block previously allocated with dtAlloc. Pairs with dtAlloc for releasing memory back to the allocator.
requirements: ptr must be a pointer to a memory block previously allocated using dtAlloc.
Passing pointers not obtained from dtAlloc results in undefined/unspecified behavior.
Behavior when passing a null pointer is not documented (unknown); avoid passing null unless implementation is known to accept it.
Do not use the memory after it has been freed (use-after-free is invalid).

functions.name: dtCreateNavMeshData
functions.signature: bool dtCreateNavMeshData(dtNavMeshCreateParams* params, unsigned char** outData, int* outDataSize);
functions.description: Builds a serialized Detour navigation mesh tile from the provided dtNavMeshCreateParams and returns it as a newly allocated byte buffer. Typical usage: fill all required fields of dtNavMeshCreateParams (polygon mesh, optional detail mesh and off-mesh connections, tile bounds/config), call this function, then add the resulting tile data to a dtNavMesh. The output buffer contains a complete Detour tile image suitable for dtNavMesh::addTile or single-tile init; on success, the caller owns the returned buffer and size. Returns true on success, false on failure. Notes: outData is modified only on success; this function allocates memory for the blob; contents are implementation-specific Detour format.
requirements: params must be non-null and fully initialized for the data you intend to build.

Polygon mesh inputs: verts points to an array of vertex coordinates of length 3*vertCount (unsigned short, in voxels); vertCount >= 3. polys points to an array sized polyCount * 2 * nvp; polyFlags points to polyCount entries; polyAreas points to polyCount entries; polyCount >= 1; nvp >= 3.

Detail mesh (optional): if provided, detailMeshes must have 4*polyCount entries; detailVerts points to 3*detailVertsCount floats; detailVertsCount >= 0; detailTris points to 4*detailTriCount bytes; detailTriCount >= 0. If any detail mesh count is non-zero, the corresponding pointer must be non-null and the arrays must meet the documented sizes.

Off-mesh connections (optional): offMeshConCount >= 0. If offMeshConCount > 0, then offMeshConVerts must have 6*offMeshConCount floats; offMeshConRad must have offMeshConCount floats; offMeshConFlags must have offMeshConCount unsigned shorts; offMeshConAreas must have offMeshConCount unsigned chars; offMeshConDir must have offMeshConCount unsigned chars; offMeshConUserID must have offMeshConCount unsigned ints.
Tile attributes: tileLayer >= 0. bmin and bmax must each contain 3 floats defining the tile AABB bounds.
General configuration: cs > 0 and ch > 0. walkableHeight, walkableRadius, walkableClimb should be set to appropriate world-unit values for the agent (non-negative).
buildBvTree indicates whether to build a BVTree; no additional requirement beyond being a valid boolean.
outData must be non-null (pointer to a pointer) and will receive a pointer to a newly allocated buffer on success; outDataSize must be non-null and will receive the size in bytes of the buffer.
The caller must check the boolean return value; only use outData/outDataSize if the function returns true.
On success, the caller is responsible for freeing *outData with the Detour allocator (dtFree) used by this library; do not free with mismatched allocators.
Inputs that are not used (e.g., optional sections with count 0) may be null; otherwise, pointers must reference readable memory of at least the sizes indicated in the struct documentation.

functions.name: dtNavMeshHeaderSwapEndian
functions.signature: bool dtNavMeshHeaderSwapEndian(unsigned char* data, const int dataSize);
functions.description: In-place endianness swap of only the dtMeshHeader portion of a serialized Detour tile buffer. Use when transporting tile data between architectures of differing endianness and you only need to adjust the header (e.g., to inspect metadata) without touching the rest of the blob. Returns true on success, false if the buffer is invalid or too small. Modifies data in place.
requirements: data must be non-null and point to a buffer that contains at least a complete serialized dtMeshHeader at its start.
dataSize must be >= the serialized size of dtMeshHeader; exact size is unknown in this context and must match the Detour version used.
The buffer must contain a valid Detour tile header in the expected layout and version; otherwise the swap may fail or produce undefined results.
This operation is in-place; calling it twice toggles the header endianness twice (effectively returning to the original).
Callers should use this only when the tile data was produced on a machine with different endianness; otherwise swapping is unnecessary.

functions.name: dtNavMeshDataSwapEndian
functions.signature: bool dtNavMeshDataSwapEndian(unsigned char* data, const int dataSize);
functions.description: In-place endianness swap of an entire serialized Detour tile buffer, including the header and all contained substructures. Use when transferring a tile blob between architectures with different endianness before feeding it to dtNavMesh. Returns true on success, false if the buffer is invalid or inconsistent. Modifies data in place.
requirements: data must be non-null and point to a complete serialized Detour tile as produced by dtCreateNavMeshData (or the equivalent Detour format).
dataSize must match the total size in bytes of the entire tile blob; if incorrect, the swap may fail or corrupt data.
The buffer layout/version must match the Detour library expectations; unknown or mismatched versions may cause failure.
This operation is in-place; calling it twice toggles endianness back to the original.
If using this full-data swap, you generally do not need to call dtNavMeshHeaderSwapEndian separately.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getObstacleRef
