functions.description: Returns the obstacle reference id corresponding to the given obstacle pointer. Useful for converting internal pointers back to stable references.
requirements: obmin must point to an obstacle owned by this dtTileCache instance.
Passing a null or foreign pointer results in an undefined/invalid reference.

functions.name: dtTileCache::init
functions.signature: dtStatus init(const dtTileCacheParams* params, struct dtTileCacheAlloc* talloc, struct dtTileCacheCompressor* tcomp, struct dtTileCacheMeshProcess* tmproc);
functions.description: Initializes the tile cache with parameters, an allocator, a compressor, and an optional mesh-process callback. Must be called before using most other APIs.
requirements: params must be a valid pointer; fields such as maxTiles and maxObstacles must be properly set.
talloc must be a valid allocator implementation for the cache lifetime.
tcomp must be a valid compressor implementation for the cache lifetime.
tmproc may be null if no mesh post-processing is needed; if non-null it must outlive or match the lifetime of the cache or be otherwise managed safely.
Must not be called more than once without destroying or resetting the cache (reinitialization semantics are unspecified).
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getTilesAt
functions.signature: int getTilesAt(const int tx, const int ty, dtCompressedTileRef* tiles, const int maxTiles) const;
functions.description: Retrieves compressed tile references at a specified tile grid coordinate (tx, ty). Returns the number of references written to the output array.
requirements: tiles must be a valid pointer to an array with capacity at least maxTiles.
maxTiles must be non-negative.
tx and ty must be valid tile coordinates for this cache's grid.
Caller should use the returned count to interpret the tiles array.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getTileAt
functions.signature: dtCompressedTile* getTileAt(const int tx, const int ty, const int tlayer);
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the compressed tile at grid coordinate (tx, ty) and layer index tlayer, or null if none exists.
requirements: tx, ty, and tlayer must be within the valid ranges of the cache configuration.
Returned pointer is owned by the cache and becomes invalid if the cache is destroyed or reinitialized.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getTileRef
functions.signature: dtCompressedTileRef getTileRef(const dtCompressedTile* tile) const;
functions.description: Returns a stable reference id for the given compressed tile pointer, allowing future lookup via getTileByRef.
requirements: tile must be a pointer to a tile owned by this dtTileCache instance.
Passing null or a foreign pointer yields an undefined/invalid reference.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getTileByRef
functions.signature: const dtCompressedTile* getTileByRef(dtCompressedTileRef ref) const;
functions.description: Looks up and returns the compressed tile corresponding to the given reference id, or null if the reference is invalid or does not point to a current tile.
requirements: ref must be a reference obtained from this dtTileCache instance (e.g., from addTile, getTileRef, or encodeTileId).
Caller must handle a possible null return if the reference is invalid or the tile is not present.

functions.name: dtTileCache::addTile
functions.signature: dtStatus addTile(unsigned char* data, const int dataSize, unsigned char flags, dtCompressedTileRef* result);
functions.description: Adds a compressed tile to the cache from a block of tile data. On success, returns a tile reference in result. Flags may include DT_COMPRESSEDTILE_FREE_DATA to transfer ownership of the memory to the cache.
requirements: data must point to a valid compressed tile data block of size dataSize bytes.
dataSize must be a positive integer representing the exact size of the tile data.
result must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the created tile reference.
flags may include DT_COMPRESSEDTILE_FREE_DATA; when set, the cache will own and free the provided memory.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.
Cache must be initialized before calling.

functions.name: dtTileCache::removeTile
functions.signature: dtStatus removeTile(dtCompressedTileRef ref, unsigned char** data, int* dataSize);
functions.description: Removes a compressed tile from the cache by reference. Optionally returns the tile data pointer and size to the caller if the cache does not own the memory, enabling the caller to free or reuse it.
requirements: ref must be a valid tile reference from this cache.
data may be null if the caller does not need the data pointer; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to receive the returned pointer.
dataSize may be null if the caller does not need the size; otherwise it must be a valid pointer to receive the size.
Ownership semantics depend on the flags used when adding the tile; if the cache owned the data (DT_COMPRESSEDTILE_FREE_DATA), it may free it internally and return null data.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::addObstacle
functions.signature: dtStatus addObstacle(const float* pos, const float radius, const float height, dtObstacleRef* result);
functions.description: Adds a cylindrical obstacle at the given position with specified radius and height. On success, returns an obstacle reference id in result and schedules affected tiles for rebuild.
requirements: pos must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats representing the center position.
radius must be a positive finite value (inferred from geometric meaning).
height must be a positive finite value (inferred from geometric meaning).
result must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the obstacle reference.
Cache must be initialized before calling.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::addBoxObstacle
functions.signature: dtStatus addBoxObstacle(const float* bmin, const float* bmax, dtObstacleRef* result);
functions.description: Adds an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB) obstacle defined by minimum and maximum corners. On success, returns an obstacle reference id in result and schedules affected tiles for rebuild.
requirements: bmin must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats (minimum corner).
bmax must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats (maximum corner).
bmin components should be less than or equal to corresponding bmax components (inferred from AABB definition).
result must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the obstacle reference.
Cache must be initialized before calling.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::removeObstacle
functions.signature: dtStatus removeObstacle(const dtObstacleRef ref);
functions.description: Queues removal of an obstacle previously added to the cache by reference id. Affected tiles will be rebuilt during update.
requirements: ref must be a valid obstacle reference from this cache.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::queryTiles
functions.signature: dtStatus queryTiles(const float* bmin, const float* bmax, dtCompressedTileRef* results, int* resultCount, const int maxResults) const;
functions.description: Queries the cache for tiles whose bounds intersect the given AABB and returns up to maxResults tile references. Writes the number of results to resultCount.
requirements: bmin must be a valid pointer to 3 floats (minimum corner).
bmax must be a valid pointer to 3 floats (maximum corner).
results must be a valid pointer to an array with capacity at least maxResults.
resultCount must be a valid non-null pointer to receive the number of results.
maxResults must be non-negative.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::update
functions.signature: dtStatus update(const float dt, class dtNavMesh* navmesh, bool* upToDate = 0);
functions.description: Processes pending obstacle add/remove requests and rebuilds affected tiles, updating the provided navmesh. Optionally reports whether the cache is fully up to date, in which case subsequent immediate calls would have no effect.
requirements: navmesh must be a valid pointer to a dtNavMesh instance to receive tile rebuilds.
upToDate may be null; if non-null it must be a valid pointer to a bool to receive the status flag.
dt is currently not used (per comment) but should be finite.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::buildNavMeshTilesAt
functions.signature: dtStatus buildNavMeshTilesAt(const int tx, const int ty, class dtNavMesh* navmesh);
functions.description: Rebuilds all navmesh tiles at the specified tile grid coordinate (tx, ty) and applies them to the provided navmesh.
requirements: tx and ty must be valid tile grid coordinates for this cache.
navmesh must be a valid pointer to a dtNavMesh instance.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::buildNavMeshTile
functions.signature: dtStatus buildNavMeshTile(const dtCompressedTileRef ref, class dtNavMesh* navmesh);
functions.description: Rebuilds and applies the navmesh tile corresponding to the given compressed tile reference.
requirements: ref must be a valid tile reference from this cache.
navmesh must be a valid pointer to a dtNavMesh instance.
Caller must check the returned dtStatus for success or failure.

functions.name: dtTileCache::calcTightTileBounds
functions.signature: void calcTightTileBounds(const struct dtTileCacheLayerHeader* header, float* bmin, float* bmax) const;
functions.description: Calculates tight axis-aligned bounds for a tile cache layer described by the header and writes them to bmin and bmax.
requirements: header must be a valid pointer to a dtTileCacheLayerHeader populated for the target tile layer.
bmin must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats to receive the minimum bound.
bmax must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats to receive the maximum bound.

functions.name: dtTileCache::getObstacleBounds
functions.signature: void getObstacleBounds(const struct dtTileCacheObstacle* ob, float* bmin, float* bmax) const;
functions.description: Computes the axis-aligned bounding box of the given obstacle (cylinder, AABB, or oriented box) and writes it to bmin and bmax.
requirements: ob must be a valid pointer to a dtTileCacheObstacle owned by this cache.
bmin must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats to receive the minimum bound.
bmax must be a valid pointer to an array of 3 floats to receive the maximum bound.

functions.name: dtTileCache::encodeTileId
functions.signature: inline dtCompressedTileRef encodeTileId(unsigned int salt, unsigned int it) const;
functions.description: Encodes a tile id reference from a salt (liveness/version) and tile index using the cache's internal bit partitioning.
requirements: salt and it must fit within the bit widths configured by this cache (m_saltBits and m_tileBits).
The resulting reference is only meaningful for this dtTileCache instance.

functions.name: dtTileCache::decodeTileIdSalt
functions.signature: inline unsigned int decodeTileIdSalt(dtCompressedTileRef ref) const;
functions.description: Extracts the salt component from an encoded tile reference.
requirements: ref must be an encoded tile reference from this dtTileCache.

functions.name: dtTileCache::decodeTileIdTile
functions.signature: inline unsigned int decodeTileIdTile(dtCompressedTileRef ref) const;
functions.description: Extracts the tile index component from an encoded tile reference.
requirements: ref must be an encoded tile reference from this dtTileCache.

functions.name: dtTileCache::encodeObstacleId
functions.signature: inline dtObstacleRef encodeObstacleId(unsigned int salt, unsigned int it) const;
functions.description: Encodes an obstacle reference id from a salt and obstacle index. Uses 16 bits for each field per comments.
requirements: salt and it must each fit within 16 bits.
The resulting reference is only meaningful for this dtTileCache instance.

functions.name: dtTileCache::decodeObstacleIdSalt
functions.signature: inline unsigned int decodeObstacleIdSalt(dtObstacleRef ref) const;
functions.description: Extracts the salt component from an encoded obstacle reference.
requirements: ref must be an encoded obstacle reference from this dtTileCache.

functions.name: dtTileCache::decodeObstacleIdObstacle
functions.signature: inline unsigned int decodeObstacleIdObstacle(dtObstacleRef ref) const;
functions.description: Extracts the obstacle index component from an encoded obstacle reference.
requirements: ref must be an encoded obstacle reference from this dtTileCache.

functions.name: dtAllocTileCache
functions.signature: dtTileCache* dtAllocTileCache();
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new dtTileCache instance on the heap.
requirements: Caller assumes ownership of the returned pointer and must eventually free it with dtFreeTileCache.
Caller must check the return for null in low-memory situations.

functions.name: dtFreeTileCache
functions.signature: void dtFreeTileCache(dtTileCache* tc);
functions.description: Frees a dtTileCache instance previously allocated with dtAllocTileCache.
requirements: tc must be a pointer returned by dtAllocTileCache or null.
After calling, the pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::dtProximityGrid
functions.signature: dtProximityGrid::dtProximityGrid();
functions.description: Default constructor. Initializes an empty proximity grid object. Actual storage is not allocated until init() succeeds. Typically created via dtAllocProximityGrid().
requirements: Object must be initialized by calling init(poolSize, cellSize) before calling any mutating or query methods (e.g., addItem, queryItems).
If constructed via new or stack, ensure a matching delete or automatic destruction, respectively; if created via dtAllocProximityGrid(), release with dtFreeProximityGrid().

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::~dtProximityGrid
functions.signature: dtProximityGrid::~dtProximityGrid();
functions.description: Destructor. Releases resources owned by the grid instance. If allocated via dtAllocProximityGrid(), prefer freeing with dtFreeProximityGrid().
requirements: Do not use the object after destruction.
Ensure no concurrent use from other threads during destruction (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::init
functions.signature: bool dtProximityGrid::init(const int poolSize, const float cellSize);
functions.description: Initializes the grid’s internal storage and cell sizing. poolSize controls the internal item pool capacity; cellSize sets the world-space cell width/height. Returns true on success.
requirements: Must be called (and return true) before addItem(), queryItems(), or other operations that depend on internal storage.
poolSize should be a positive integer; zero or negative sizes are invalid/unspecified.
cellSize should be a positive finite float; zero or negative sizes are invalid/unspecified.
Re-initializing an already-initialized instance may clear/replace previous data; behavior beyond allocation is not specified.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::clear
functions.signature: void dtProximityGrid::clear();
functions.description: Clears all items from the grid, leaving it initialized and ready for reuse with the same configuration (cell size and pool).
requirements: init() must have succeeded prior to calling clear().
After clear(), previously returned pointers (e.g., from getBounds()) remain valid as they point to internal state, but the logical contents (items) are removed.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::addItem
functions.signature: void dtProximityGrid::addItem(const unsigned short id, const float minx, const float miny, const float maxx, const float maxy);
functions.description: Adds an item identified by id and described by an axis-aligned bounding box [minx,miny]..[maxx,maxy] into the proximity grid. The item will occupy all cells overlapped by the AABB.
requirements: init() must have succeeded before calling addItem().
minx <= maxx and miny <= maxy; coordinates are in the same world-space units as the grid’s cell size.
The number of items inserted must not exceed the configured poolSize; exceeding may fail internally (behavior unspecified here).
id is a 16-bit unsigned value; caller is responsible for ensuring uniqueness or handling duplicates as needed (behavior on duplicates unspecified).

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::queryItems
functions.signature: int dtProximityGrid::queryItems(const float minx, const float miny, const float maxx, const float maxy, unsigned short* ids, const int maxIds) const;
functions.description: Queries the grid for items overlapping the axis-aligned rectangle [minx,miny]..[maxx,maxy]. Writes up to maxIds item IDs into ids. Returns the number of IDs written (and possibly the total found, clipped to maxIds; exact semantics not documented).
requirements: init() must have succeeded before calling queryItems().
minx <= maxx and miny <= maxy; coordinates are in the same world-space units used by addItem().
ids must be a valid, writable array when maxIds > 0; can be null if maxIds == 0.
maxIds must be >= 0.
Caller must handle that the return value may be limited by maxIds; if more items exist than maxIds, some may be omitted.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::getItemCountAt
functions.signature: int dtProximityGrid::getItemCountAt(const int x, const int y) const;
functions.description: Returns the number of items currently mapped to the grid cell at integer coordinates (x, y). Coordinates are in cell-space, not world-space.
requirements: init() must have succeeded before calling getItemCountAt().
x and y should refer to valid cell coordinates within the grid’s current bounds; use getBounds() to determine valid ranges.
Behavior for out-of-bounds coordinates is unspecified.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::getBounds
functions.signature: const int* dtProximityGrid::getBounds() const;
functions.description: Returns a pointer to an internal array of 4 integers describing the grid bounds in cell coordinates. Typical convention is [minx, miny, maxx, maxy], but exact ordering is not documented in this header.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid while the dtProximityGrid object remains alive and unmodified by operations that would change bounds; do not store beyond the object’s lifetime.
Do not modify the memory pointed to (const int*).
Call init() before relying on the bounds; contents are undefined before initialization.

functions.name: dtProximityGrid::getCellSize
functions.signature: float dtProximityGrid::getCellSize() const;
functions.description: Returns the current cell size in world-space units configured during init().
requirements: Call init() successfully before relying on the returned value; value is undefined before initialization.

functions.name: dtAllocProximityGrid
functions.signature: dtProximityGrid* dtAllocProximityGrid();
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new dtProximityGrid instance using the library’s allocation strategy. Call init() on the returned object before use. Free with dtFreeProximityGrid().
requirements: Check the return value for null indicating allocation failure before use.
Must be paired with dtFreeProximityGrid(ptr) to avoid leaks.

functions.name: dtFreeProximityGrid
functions.signature: void dtFreeProximityGrid(dtProximityGrid* ptr);
functions.description: Frees a dtProximityGrid previously created by dtAllocProximityGrid(). Performs destruction and deallocation using the library’s strategy.
requirements: ptr must either be a valid pointer returned by dtAllocProximityGrid() or null (null-handling not documented; prefer passing a valid pointer or explicitly check for null).
Do not pass a pointer allocated with new or to a stack/local object; use delete or automatic destruction for those instead.
Do not call more than once on the same pointer (no double-free).
Ensure no other threads are using the object when freeing (thread-safety not specified).

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::dtLocalBoundary
functions.signature: dtLocalBoundary::dtLocalBoundary()
functions.description: Constructs an empty local boundary container that tracks nearby wall segments around a center point on a Detour navmesh. Initially no center, segments, or polygon refs are stored.
requirements: No arguments or preconditions.
Object is non-copyable (copy constructor and assignment are disabled).

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::~dtLocalBoundary
functions.signature: dtLocalBoundary::~dtLocalBoundary()
functions.description: Destroys the local boundary object and releases any internal state. No external resources are owned beyond internal arrays, so typical usage is stack or member lifetime management.
requirements: Must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::reset
functions.signature: void dtLocalBoundary::reset()
functions.description: Clears the stored center, segments, and polygon references, returning the boundary to an empty state. Use when reinitializing or after invalidation.
requirements: Can be called at any time on a valid dtLocalBoundary instance.
All previously returned pointers from getCenter()/getSegment() become stale after reset and must not be used.

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::update
functions.signature: void dtLocalBoundary::update(dtPolyRef ref, const float* pos, const float collisionQueryRange, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Rebuilds the local boundary around a given position on the navmesh. It queries nearby polygons starting from ref within collisionQueryRange using navquery/filter, extracts wall segments, stores up to an internal maximum, and updates the center to pos. Intended for per-frame or periodic updates when an agent moves.
requirements: ref should be a valid polygon reference from the same navmesh used by navquery.
pos must be a non-null pointer to an array of 3 floats representing the world-space position (x,y,z).
collisionQueryRange should be a positive finite distance specifying the neighborhood search radius.
navquery must be a non-null pointer to an initialized dtNavMeshQuery associated with a valid dtNavMesh.
filter must be a non-null pointer to a valid dtQueryFilter instance appropriate for the query.
On success, previously returned pointers from getCenter()/getSegment() are updated; callers must not retain old pointers across updates.
The function may prune to an internal maximum of segments (MAX_LOCAL_SEGS=8) and polygons (MAX_LOCAL_POLYS=16); callers should not assume more than these will be stored.

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::isValid
functions.signature: bool dtLocalBoundary::isValid(dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Checks whether the cached local boundary state (center, polygon refs, segments) is still valid for the given navquery and filter. Typical usage is to verify the boundary after topology changes or when continuing to use previously cached data.
requirements: navquery must be a non-null pointer to an initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a non-null pointer to a valid dtQueryFilter.
Caller should handle a false return by calling reset() and/or update() before relying on boundary data.

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::getCenter
functions.signature: const float* dtLocalBoundary::getCenter() const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current center position of the local boundary as 3 floats (x,y,z). The data is owned by the object and remains valid until the next update(), reset(), or object destruction.
requirements: Must be called on a valid dtLocalBoundary instance.
Returned pointer must not be stored beyond the next update() or reset().

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::getSegmentCount
functions.signature: int dtLocalBoundary::getSegmentCount() const
functions.description: Returns the number of stored wall segments currently in the local boundary, up to an internal maximum (8).
requirements: Must be called on a valid dtLocalBoundary instance.
Result is in the range [0, 8]. Use this value to bound indices passed to getSegment().

functions.name: dtLocalBoundary::getSegment
functions.signature: const float* dtLocalBoundary::getSegment(int i) const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the i-th stored wall segment as 6 floats representing segment start and end (x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1). The memory is owned by the object and valid until the next update(), reset(), or object destruction.
requirements: i must be in range 0 <= i < getSegmentCount().
Must be called on a valid dtLocalBoundary instance.
Returned pointer must not be stored beyond the next update() or reset().

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData()
functions.description: Default constructor for the obstacle avoidance debug data container. Prepares an empty object to be initialized via init() before use.
requirements: Must call init(int maxSamples) before adding samples or reading sample data.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::~dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::~dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData()
functions.description: Destructor for the debug data container. Releases any resources owned by the instance.
requirements: All external references to internal buffers (e.g., from getSampleVelocity()) must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::init
functions.signature: bool dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::init(const int maxSamples)
functions.description: Allocates/initializes internal storage for up to maxSamples debug samples used during obstacle avoidance velocity sampling.
requirements: maxSamples must be a non-negative integer.
Must be called before addSample(), normalizeSamples(), or any getters.
If called multiple times, previous internal buffers may be replaced; previously returned pointers from getters may be invalidated.
Returns false on allocation/init failure; callers must check the return value before further use.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::reset
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::reset()
functions.description: Clears current samples and resets internal counters while keeping allocated capacity from init(). Use before starting a new sampling run.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called prior to reset().

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::addSample
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::addSample(const float* vel, const float ssize, const float pen, const float vpen, const float vcpen, const float spen, const float tpen)
functions.description: Adds a single sampled velocity and associated penalty components to the debug data set for later inspection/visualization or analysis.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called before adding samples.
vel must point to an array of at least 3 floats representing the velocity vector (vx, vy, vz).
ssize, pen, vpen, vcpen, spen, tpen are scalars describing sample size and penalty breakdown; their interpretation is library-defined.
The number of added samples must not exceed the capacity specified by init(maxSamples). Exceeding capacity is undefined and may be ignored or overwrite data depending on implementation.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::normalizeSamples
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::normalizeSamples()
functions.description: Normalizes stored penalty values across samples for easier comparison/visualization.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.
Should be called after adding samples and before reading normalized penalties from getters.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCount
functions.signature: int dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCount() const
functions.description: Returns the number of samples currently stored.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleVelocity
functions.signature: const float* dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleVelocity(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the 3-float velocity vector of the i-th sample.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.
i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).
The returned pointer remains valid until the next reset(), init(), destruction, or any operation that modifies internal storage.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleSize
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleSize(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the sample size value associated with the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSamplePenalty
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSamplePenalty(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the total penalty for the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleDesiredVelocityPenalty
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleDesiredVelocityPenalty(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the desired-velocity component of the penalty for the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCurrentVelocityPenalty
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCurrentVelocityPenalty(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the current-velocity component of the penalty for the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSamplePreferredSidePenalty
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSamplePreferredSidePenalty(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the preferred-side component of the penalty for the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCollisionTimePenalty
functions.signature: float dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData::getSampleCollisionTimePenalty(const int i) const
functions.description: Returns the time-of-impact (collision time) component of the penalty for the i-th sample.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getSampleCount()).

functions.name: dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceDebugData
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData* dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceDebugData()
functions.description: Allocates a new dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData instance using the library's allocator.
requirements: Caller must check the returned pointer for null (allocation failure).
The returned object must be freed with dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceDebugData().
After allocation, init() must be called before use.

functions.name: dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceDebugData
functions.signature: void dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceDebugData(dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData* ptr)
functions.description: Frees a dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData instance allocated with dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceDebugData().
requirements: ptr may be null (a no-op) or a pointer returned by dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceDebugData().
After this call, ptr must not be used.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery()
functions.description: Default constructor for the obstacle avoidance query object. Sets up an empty query to be initialized with init() before use.
requirements: Must call init(int maxCircles, int maxSegments) before adding obstacles or sampling velocities.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::~dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::~dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery()
functions.description: Destructor for the query object. Releases resources owned by the instance.
requirements: Do not use pointers returned by getObstacleCircle()/getObstacleSegment() after destruction.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::init
functions.signature: bool dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::init(const int maxCircles, const int maxSegments)
functions.description: Allocates/initializes internal storage for up to maxCircles circular obstacles and maxSegments segment obstacles, preparing the query for use.
requirements: maxCircles and maxSegments must be non-negative integers.
Must be called before addCircle(), addSegment(), or sampling methods.
Returns false on allocation/init failure; callers must check the return value.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::reset
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::reset()
functions.description: Clears the current obstacle lists and internal state while retaining allocated capacity from init(). Call before repopulating obstacles for a new query.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called prior to reset().

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::addCircle
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::addCircle(const float* pos, const float rad, const float* vel, const float* dvel)
functions.description: Adds a circular obstacle with position, radius, current velocity, and desired velocity to the query's obstacle set.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.
pos must point to at least 3 floats (x,y,z).
vel must point to at least 3 floats (vx,vy,vz).
dvel must point to at least 3 floats (desired velocity).
rad should be non-negative.
The number of circles added must not exceed the capacity specified by init(maxCircles).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::addSegment
functions.signature: void dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::addSegment(const float* p, const float* q)
functions.description: Adds a line-segment obstacle defined by endpoints p and q to the query's obstacle set.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.
p must point to at least 3 floats (x,y,z).
q must point to at least 3 floats (x,y,z).
The number of segments added must not exceed the capacity specified by init(maxSegments).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::sampleVelocityGrid
functions.signature: int dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::sampleVelocityGrid(const float* pos, const float rad, const float vmax, const float* vel, const float* dvel, float* nvel, const dtObstacleAvoidanceParams* params, dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData* debug = 0)
functions.description: Samples candidate velocities on a grid to find a near-optimal collision-free velocity nvel for an agent at pos with radius rad, given current velocity vel, desired velocity dvel, and parameters. Optionally records debug data.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called and the obstacle set prepared via addCircle()/addSegment() as needed.
pos must point to at least 3 floats.
vel must point to at least 3 floats.
dvel must point to at least 3 floats.
nvel must point to writable storage for at least 3 floats to receive the selected velocity.
params must be a valid, non-null pointer to a filled dtObstacleAvoidanceParams structure.
rad and vmax should be non-negative.
If provided, debug must point to an initialized dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData (init() called).
Return value is an int; its exact meaning is library-defined (e.g., number of samples evaluated). Callers should not assume more without consulting implementation.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::sampleVelocityAdaptive
functions.signature: int dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::sampleVelocityAdaptive(const float* pos, const float rad, const float vmax, const float* vel, const float* dvel, float* nvel, const dtObstacleAvoidanceParams* params, dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData* debug = 0)
functions.description: Samples candidate velocities using an adaptive pattern to find a near-optimal collision-free velocity nvel for an agent at pos with radius rad, given current velocity vel, desired velocity dvel, and parameters. Optionally records debug data.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called and obstacles added as needed.
pos, vel, dvel must each point to at least 3 floats.
nvel must point to writable storage for at least 3 floats.
params must be a valid, non-null pointer to a filled dtObstacleAvoidanceParams.
rad and vmax should be non-negative.
If provided, debug must point to an initialized dtObstacleAvoidanceDebugData (init() called).
Return value is an int; its exact meaning is library-defined (e.g., number of samples evaluated).

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleCircleCount
functions.signature: int dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleCircleCount() const
functions.description: Returns the number of circular obstacles currently stored in the query.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleCircle
functions.signature: const dtObstacleCircle* dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleCircle(const int i)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the i-th circular obstacle currently stored.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getObstacleCircleCount()).
The returned pointer remains valid until the next reset(), init(), modification of the obstacle list, or destruction of the query object.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleSegmentCount
functions.signature: int dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleSegmentCount() const
functions.description: Returns the number of segment obstacles currently stored in the query.
requirements: init() must have been successfully called.

functions.name: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleSegment
functions.signature: const dtObstacleSegment* dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery::getObstacleSegment(const int i)
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the i-th segment obstacle currently stored.
requirements: i must be in the range [0, getObstacleSegmentCount()).
The returned pointer remains valid until the next reset(), init(), modification of the obstacle list, or destruction of the query object.

functions.name: dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceQuery
functions.signature: dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery* dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceQuery()
functions.description: Allocates a new dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery instance using the library's allocator.
requirements: Caller must check the returned pointer for null (allocation failure).
The returned object must be freed with dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceQuery().
After allocation, init() must be called before use.

functions.name: dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceQuery
functions.signature: void dtFreeObstacleAvoidanceQuery(dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery* ptr)
functions.description: Frees a dtObstacleAvoidanceQuery instance allocated with dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceQuery().
requirements: ptr may be null (a no-op) or a pointer returned by dtAllocObstacleAvoidanceQuery().
After this call, ptr must not be used.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::dtPathCorridor
functions.signature: dtPathCorridor::dtPathCorridor()
functions.description: Constructor. Initializes an empty/detached path corridor object. Intended to be followed by init() to allocate internal path storage before use.
requirements: Must call init(maxPath) before using methods that depend on internal path storage (e.g., setCorridor, findCorners, moves).
Object must remain alive for the duration of any operations that reference its internal buffers.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::~dtPathCorridor
functions.signature: dtPathCorridor::~dtPathCorridor()
functions.description: Destructor. Releases resources owned by the path corridor instance (e.g., internal path buffer).
requirements: No requirements on callers beyond ensuring no further use after destruction.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::init
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::init(const int maxPath)
functions.description: Allocates the corridor's internal path buffer to hold up to maxPath polygon references. Returns true on success.
requirements: maxPath must be a positive integer (> 0).
Must be called before operations that require an allocated path buffer (e.g., setCorridor, findCorners, movePosition/TargetPosition, optimization functions).

The dtPathCorridor instance must not already rely on an existing buffer that the caller expects to preserve; calling init() may reallocate/clear internal state (details of prior contents are unknown).

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::reset
functions.signature: void dtPathCorridor::reset(dtPolyRef ref, const float* pos)
functions.description: Resets the corridor so that it starts at the polygon ref containing pos, and sets the current position to pos. Any existing path is reset to this start.
requirements: ref must be a valid dtPolyRef of a polygon that contains the point pos.
pos must point to an array of at least 3 floats representing (x, y, z).
init(maxPath) should have been called previously so the corridor has storage for its path.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::findCorners
functions.signature: int dtPathCorridor::findCorners(float* cornerVerts, unsigned char* cornerFlags, dtPolyRef* cornerPolys, const int maxCorners, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Computes the straightened path corners from the corridor's current position toward its target. Outputs corner vertices, flags, and polygon refs up to maxCorners. Returns the number of corners written.
requirements: cornerVerts must point to writable storage for at least 3*maxCorners floats.
cornerFlags must point to writable storage for at least maxCorners bytes.
cornerPolys must point to writable storage for at least maxCorners dtPolyRef entries.
maxCorners must be non-negative; buffers must match this capacity.
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery instance associated with the relevant navmesh.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter pointer.
The corridor should have a valid path set (e.g., via reset/setCorridor) for meaningful results.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::optimizePathVisibility
functions.signature: void dtPathCorridor::optimizePathVisibility(const float* next, const float pathOptimizationRange, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Attempts to locally optimize the corridor by straightening/short-cutting toward the point 'next' if it is visible from the current position within the given range.
requirements: next must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
pathOptimizationRange must be greater than 0.
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor should have a valid path set and a current position (via reset/setCorridor).

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::optimizePathTopology
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::optimizePathTopology(dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Attempts partial replanning/topology optimization of the corridor within a local area to improve path quality. Returns true if an optimization was made.
requirements: navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor should already have a valid path set.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::moveOverOffmeshConnection
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::moveOverOffmeshConnection(dtPolyRef offMeshConRef, dtPolyRef* refs, float* startPos, float* endPos, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery)
functions.description: Attempts to traverse an off-mesh connection identified by offMeshConRef, updating the corridor/path and providing start and end positions for the traversal. Returns true on success. Detailed outputs format/length for refs are not documented in this header and are unknown.
requirements: offMeshConRef must reference a valid off-mesh connection on the current path.
refs must point to writable storage; capacity requirements are not documented here (likely holds polygon refs involved in the transition; exact count unknown).
startPos and endPos must point to arrays of at least 3 floats each to receive positions.
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
The corridor should be positioned such that the off-mesh connection is the next transition; otherwise the call may fail.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::fixPathStart
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::fixPathStart(dtPolyRef safeRef, const float* safePos)
functions.description: Attempts to repair the beginning of the path corridor so it starts from the provided safe polygon and position. Returns true if the start was fixed/updated.
requirements: safeRef should be a valid polygon reference that contains safePos.
safePos must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
The corridor should have been initialized and have a path that can be adjusted.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::trimInvalidPath
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::trimInvalidPath(dtPolyRef safeRef, const float* safePos, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Trims or repairs the corridor path to remove invalid polygons, ensuring it starts at safeRef/safePos if necessary. Returns true if the path remains or becomes valid after trimming.
requirements: safeRef should be a valid polygon reference, typically known to be valid for safePos.
safePos must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor should have been initialized; path content may be modified by this call.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::isValid
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::isValid(const int maxLookAhead, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Checks whether the corridor path's polygon references remain valid over the first maxLookAhead polygons. Returns true if valid.
requirements: maxLookAhead must be non-negative.
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor should have an existing path; if empty, validity may trivially pass or fail depending on implementation (unspecified here).

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::movePosition
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::movePosition(const float* npos, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Moves the corridor's current position toward npos, adjusting the corridor to remain valid with respect to the navmesh. Returns true on success.
requirements: npos must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor must be initialized and associated with a valid starting polygon (e.g., via reset).

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::moveTargetPosition
functions.signature: bool dtPathCorridor::moveTargetPosition(const float* npos, dtNavMeshQuery* navquery, const dtQueryFilter* filter)
functions.description: Moves the corridor's target toward npos, updating the corridor path as needed. Returns true on success.
requirements: npos must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
navquery must be a valid, initialized dtNavMeshQuery.
filter must be a valid dtQueryFilter.
The corridor must be initialized and have a valid path/target to adjust.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::setCorridor
functions.signature: void dtPathCorridor::setCorridor(const float* target, const dtPolyRef* polys, const int npath)
functions.description: Loads a new path and target into the corridor. The target lies within the last polygon of the provided path.
requirements: target must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z) within the last polygon of polys.
polys must point to an array of at least npath dtPolyRef elements representing a contiguous corridor.
npath must be non-negative and should not exceed the capacity specified by init(maxPath).
The corridor must have been initialized with sufficient maxPath to hold npath entries.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getPos
functions.signature: const float* dtPathCorridor::getPos() const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current position (x, y, z) within the corridor's first polygon.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the dtPathCorridor instance remains alive and its internal buffers are not reinitialized.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getTarget
functions.signature: const float* dtPathCorridor::getTarget() const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the current target position (x, y, z) within the corridor's last polygon.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as the dtPathCorridor instance remains alive and its internal buffers are not reinitialized.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getFirstPoly
functions.signature: dtPolyRef dtPathCorridor::getFirstPoly() const
functions.description: Returns the polygon reference id of the first polygon in the corridor (containing the current position), or zero if there is no path.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getLastPoly
functions.signature: dtPolyRef dtPathCorridor::getLastPoly() const
functions.description: Returns the polygon reference id of the last polygon in the corridor (containing the target), or zero if there is no path.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getPath
functions.signature: const dtPolyRef* dtPathCorridor::getPath() const
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the internal array of polygon references representing the corridor path.
requirements: The returned pointer is valid while the dtPathCorridor instance remains alive and until the path is modified or the buffer is reallocated.
Use getPathCount() to determine the number of valid entries.

functions.name: dtPathCorridor::getPathCount
functions.signature: int dtPathCorridor::getPathCount() const
functions.description: Returns the current number of polygons in the corridor's path.

functions.name: dtMergeCorridorStartMoved
functions.signature: int dtMergeCorridorStartMoved(dtPolyRef* path, const int npath, const int maxPath, const dtPolyRef* visited, const int nvisited)
functions.description: Merges a set of recently visited polygons into the start of an existing corridor path after the start position has moved, updating the path to remain contiguous. Returns an integer result (commonly the new path length). Exact merge behavior is inferred from the name; detailed rules are not specified in this header.
requirements: path must point to a writable array of dtPolyRef with capacity at least maxPath.
npath must be between 0 and maxPath.
visited must point to an array of nvisited dtPolyRef entries representing the visited sequence to merge.
nvisited must be non-negative.
Behavior on overlaps and the exact return value semantics are not specified here; callers should be prepared to use the returned int as the resulting path length.

functions.name: dtMergeCorridorEndMoved
functions.signature: int dtMergeCorridorEndMoved(dtPolyRef* path, const int npath, const int maxPath, const dtPolyRef* visited, const int nvisited)
functions.description: Merges a set of recently visited polygons into the end of an existing corridor path after the end/target has moved, updating the path to remain contiguous. Returns an integer result (commonly the new path length). Exact merge behavior is inferred from the name; detailed rules are not specified in this header.
requirements: path must point to a writable array of dtPolyRef with capacity at least maxPath.
npath must be between 0 and maxPath.
visited must point to an array of nvisited dtPolyRef entries representing the visited sequence to merge.
nvisited must be non-negative.
Callers should treat the return value as the resulting path length; exact semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: dtMergeCorridorStartShortcut
functions.signature: int dtMergeCorridorStartShortcut(dtPolyRef* path, const int npath, const int maxPath, const dtPolyRef* visited, const int nvisited)
functions.description: Attempts to shortcut portions near the start of the path by merging a visited sequence into the corridor, potentially removing loops or redundancies. Returns an integer result (commonly the new path length). Exact behavior is inferred from the name; details are not specified in this header.
requirements: path must point to a writable array of dtPolyRef with capacity at least maxPath.
npath must be between 0 and maxPath.
visited must point to an array of nvisited dtPolyRef entries representing the visited sequence to consider for shortcutting.
nvisited must be non-negative.
Callers should treat the return value as the resulting path length; exact semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::dtPathQueue
functions.signature: dtPathQueue::dtPathQueue();
functions.description: Default constructor for dtPathQueue. Initializes an empty path request queue and internal members. Use init() before submitting any requests.
requirements: Must call init(...) successfully before calling update(), request(), getRequestStatus(), or getPathResult().
Object must not be copied (copy constructor is disabled).

functions.name: dtPathQueue::~dtPathQueue
functions.signature: dtPathQueue::~dtPathQueue();
functions.description: Destructor for dtPathQueue. Cleans up internal queue/resources. After destruction, the object must not be used.
requirements: All outstanding uses of the object must cease before destruction.
Do not call any member functions after the object has been destroyed.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::init
functions.signature: bool dtPathQueue::init(const int maxPathSize, const int maxSearchNodeCount, dtNavMesh* nav);
functions.description: Initializes the path queue with path/result buffer sizing and attaches it to a navmesh. Expected usage: call once after construction, before submitting requests.
requirements: nav must point to a valid dtNavMesh instance that remains alive for the lifetime of the queue or until reinitialized.
maxPathSize must be a positive integer (capacity for returned paths).
maxSearchNodeCount must be a positive integer (internal search node limit).
Must be called before request(), update(), getRequestStatus(), or getPathResult().
Return value must be checked; if false, initialization failed and the object must not be used.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::update
functions.signature: void dtPathQueue::update(const int maxIters);
functions.description: Advances processing of queued pathfinding requests, performing up to maxIters iterations of work. Call repeatedly (e.g., per frame) to progress requests.
requirements: init() must have completed successfully before calling.
maxIters should be a non-negative integer; values <= 0 perform no work.
Thread-safety/ reentrancy is unknown; call from a single thread unless otherwise guaranteed.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::request
functions.signature: dtPathQueueRef dtPathQueue::request(dtPolyRef startRef, dtPolyRef endRef, const float* startPos, const float* endPos, const dtQueryFilter* filter);
functions.description: Enqueues an asynchronous pathfinding request from startRef/startPos to endRef/endPos using the provided query filter. Returns a handle (dtPathQueueRef) that can be used to query status and retrieve the result.
requirements: init() must have completed successfully before calling.
startRef and endRef must be valid dtPolyRef references on the attached dtNavMesh.
startPos and endPos must each point to arrays of at least 3 floats representing positions within the navmesh.
filter must point to a valid dtQueryFilter that remains alive and unchanged until the request completes (comment notes this is potentially dangerous).
Queue capacity is limited (MAX_QUEUE == 8). If the queue is full, the function may fail or return DT_PATHQ_INVALID (0).
The returned handle must be checked; DT_PATHQ_INVALID (0) indicates failure to enqueue.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::getRequestStatus
functions.signature: dtStatus dtPathQueue::getRequestStatus(dtPathQueueRef ref) const;
functions.description: Retrieves the processing status (dtStatus) of a previously enqueued request identified by ref. Use to poll for completion or failure.
requirements: ref must be a valid dtPathQueueRef returned from request().
DT_PATHQ_INVALID (0) is not a valid request handle and will result in an error status.
Call only after init() has succeeded.
Interpretation of dtStatus flags follows the Detour convention (success/failure/in-progress).

functions.name: dtPathQueue::getPathResult
functions.signature: dtStatus dtPathQueue::getPathResult(dtPathQueueRef ref, dtPolyRef* path, int* pathSize, const int maxPath);
functions.description: Retrieves the resulting path for a completed request identified by ref. Writes up to maxPath polygon references into path and sets pathSize. Returns a dtStatus indicating success or error.
requirements: ref must be a valid dtPathQueueRef for a previously enqueued request.
The request should be completed (check getRequestStatus()) before retrieving results; calling early may return an in-progress or failure status.
path must point to writable storage for at least maxPath dtPolyRef entries.
pathSize must be a valid, writable pointer to an int to receive the number of path polys written.
maxPath must be a positive integer and should be >= the max path size configured at init() to avoid truncation.
Call only after init() has succeeded.

functions.name: dtPathQueue::getNavQuery
functions.signature: inline const dtNavMeshQuery* dtPathQueue::getNavQuery() const;
functions.description: Returns the internal dtNavMeshQuery used by the queue. Useful for advanced inspection or configuration. The pointer is const and may be null if not initialized.
requirements: init() must have been called to guarantee a non-null pointer; otherwise the returned pointer may be null.
The returned pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Do not retain and use the pointer after the dtPathQueue is destroyed.

functions.name: duDebugDraw::~duDebugDraw
functions.signature: virtual ~duDebugDraw() = 0;
functions.description: Pure-virtual destructor for the abstract debug draw interface. Ensures proper cleanup through base-class pointers.
requirements: Class is abstract; cannot be instantiated directly.
Derived classes must provide a definition (even if empty) for the pure-virtual destructor to allow deletion through base pointer.
Objects should be destroyed via delete on a pointer to duDebugDraw or a derived type.

functions.name: duDebugDraw::depthMask
functions.signature: virtual void depthMask(bool state) = 0;
functions.description: Enable or disable depth writes in the debug drawing backend. Intended to control whether primitives affect the depth buffer during subsequent draws.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
May be called at any time on a valid duDebugDraw instance.

functions.name: duDebugDraw::texture
functions.signature: virtual void texture(bool state) = 0;
functions.description: Enable or disable texturing for subsequent debug drawing. Implementations may bind or unbind textures accordingly.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
Call on a valid duDebugDraw instance before issuing textured vertices (i.e., the uv-enabled vertex overloads).

functions.name: duDebugDraw::begin
functions.signature: virtual void begin(duDebugDrawPrimitives prim, float size = 1.0f) = 0;
functions.description: Begin submitting a sequence of debug-draw primitives of the given type. The size parameter controls point size or line width when applicable.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
Must be paired with a matching end() call before starting another primitive sequence.
size applies to DU_DRAW_POINTS and DU_DRAW_LINES; has no effect for filled primitives.
Call only on a valid duDebugDraw instance.

functions.name: duDebugDraw::vertex
functions.signature: virtual void vertex(const float* pos, unsigned int color) = 0;
functions.description: Submit a single vertex to the current primitive stream using a 3-float position array and ARGB color.
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
Must be called between begin(...) and end().
pos must point to at least 3 floats (x, y, z).
color is a 32-bit packed color (duRGBA format: R in bits 0–7, G 8–15, B 16–23, A 24–31).

functions.name: duDebugDraw::end
functions.signature: virtual void end() = 0;
functions.description: End submission of the current primitive sequence started by begin().
requirements: Must be implemented by derived classes.
Must only be called after a matching begin(...).

functions.name: duDebugDraw::areaToCol
functions.signature: virtual unsigned int areaToCol(unsigned int area);
functions.description: Compute a display color for a logical area identifier. Used to give consistent colors to areas when drawing. Implementation is provided out-of-line.
requirements: area is an application-defined area id.
Returns a 32-bit packed color (duRGBA layout).
Call on a valid duDebugDraw instance; may be overridden by derived classes.

functions.name: duRGBA
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duRGBA(int r, int g, int b, int a);
functions.description: Pack 8-bit channel components into a 32-bit color in RGBA byte order (R in bits 0–7, G 8–15, B 16–23, A 24–31).
requirements: r, g, b, a are expected to be in the range [0, 255]; values outside will be truncated to 8 bits.
Returns a 32-bit packed color suitable for other debug draw APIs here.

functions.name: duRGBAf
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duRGBAf(float fr, float fg, float fb, float fa);
functions.description: Convert normalized float color channels to a packed 32-bit RGBA color by multiplying by 255 and clamping via cast to unsigned char.
requirements: fr, fg, fb, fa are expected to be normalized floats in [0.0f, 1.0f]; values outside will be truncated when cast to unsigned char.
Returns a 32-bit packed color compatible with duRGBA layout.

functions.name: duIntToCol
functions.signature: unsigned int duIntToCol(int i, int a);
functions.description: Map an integer index to a pseudo-random but stable RGB color and apply the specified alpha. Exact mapping is defined out of line.
requirements: a is expected to be in [0, 255] as an alpha channel value.
i can be any integer; mapping behavior is implementation-defined.
Returns a 32-bit packed color (duRGBA layout).

functions.name: duMultCol
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duMultCol(const unsigned int col, const unsigned int d);
functions.description: Multiply the RGB channels of a packed color by a scalar factor d/256, preserving alpha. Useful for dimming or tinting.
requirements: col is a 32-bit packed color in duRGBA layout.
d is treated as an 8.8 fixed-point scale; typical range is [0, 255] for meaningful results.

functions.name: duDarkenCol
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duDarkenCol(unsigned int col);
functions.description: Return a darkened version of the color by halving each RGB channel; alpha is preserved.
requirements: col is a 32-bit packed color in duRGBA layout.

functions.name: duLerpCol
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duLerpCol(unsigned int ca, unsigned int cb, unsigned int u);
functions.description: Linearly interpolate between two packed colors ca and cb by factor u/255 per channel, including alpha.
requirements: ca and cb are 32-bit packed colors in duRGBA layout.
u is an interpolation factor in [0, 255] where 0 selects ca and 255 selects cb.

functions.name: duTransCol
functions.signature: inline unsigned int duTransCol(unsigned int c, unsigned int a);
functions.description: Replace the alpha channel of packed color c with a (0–255) while keeping RGB intact.
requirements: c is a 32-bit packed color in duRGBA layout.
a is expected to be in [0, 255]; higher bits are truncated.

functions.name: duCalcBoxColors
functions.signature: void duCalcBoxColors(unsigned int* colors, unsigned int colTop, unsigned int colSide);
functions.description: Compute per-face colors for a box, given a top-face color and a side-face color. Writes the results into the provided colors array.
requirements: colors must point to a writable array large enough to hold all face colors; boxes have 6 faces, so provide space for at least 6 unsigned int entries.
colTop and colSide are packed colors in duRGBA layout.

functions.name: duDebugDrawCylinderWire
functions.signature: void duDebugDrawCylinderWire(struct duDebugDraw* dd, float minx, float miny, float minz, float maxx, float maxy, float maxz, unsigned int col, const float lineWidth);

functions.name: duDebugDrawTriMesh
functions.signature: void duDebugDrawTriMesh(struct duDebugDraw* dd, const float* verts, int nverts, const int* tris, const float* normals, int ntris, const unsigned char* flags, const float texScale);
functions.description: Renders a triangle mesh for debugging using the provided debug-draw interface. Intended to visualize raw geometry (e.g., input to Recast). Vertices and triangle indices are read-only; optional normals and per-triangle flags can influence shading/coloring. texScale typically scales any procedural texturing used by the debug renderer.
requirements: dd must be a valid, initialized duDebugDraw implementation pointer (non-null).
verts must point to an array of 3*nverts floats representing xyz positions; nverts >= 0.
tris must point to an array of 3*ntris ints indexing into verts; ntris >= 0.
If normals is non-null, it must reference normals compatible with the mesh (exact convention is unknown from this header).
If flags is non-null, it must reference at least ntris entries (unsigned char each) used for per-triangle visualization; exact semantics are unknown.
texScale should be a finite float; typical positive values control texture density.
Triangle indices in tris must be within [0, nverts).

requirements: dd must be a valid, initialized duDebugDraw implementation pointer (non-null).
verts must point to an array of 3*nverts floats representing xyz positions; nverts >= 0.
tris must point to an array of 3*ntris ints indexing into verts; ntris >= 0.
If normals is non-null, it must reference normals compatible with the mesh (exact convention is unknown from this header).
Triangle indices in tris must be within [0, nverts).
walkableSlopeAngle should be a finite angle in degrees; typical valid range is [0, 90], but exact enforcement is unknown from this header.
texScale should be a finite float; typical positive values control texture density.

#    unsigned ints with interesting values.
# 3) Keep buffer <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Strategy:
# - Emit a header of several 32-bit unsigned ints with interesting values for category and number.
# - Emit a pool of multiple null-terminated strings likely to exercise logging variability: empty,

#   used as format (they are passed as %s argument, safe), and path-like/edge-case strings.
# - Randomize order/selection seeded by input seed.
#
# Note: The format string passed to rcContext::log is fixed to "%s %d" in the stub, so our provided
# string should be valid bytes and not contain embedded null (except terminator). We ensure null-terminated.


def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack('<I', x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _choose_interesting_uints(rng: random.Random) -> List[int]:
    vals = [
        0, 1, 2, 3, 4,
        0xFFFFFFFF, 0x7FFFFFFF, 0x80000000,
        10, 42, 100, 255, 256, 1024, 65535, 65536,
    ]
    # Add some random values as well
    for _ in range(8):
        vals.append(rng.getrandbits(32))
    rng.shuffle(vals)
    return vals


def _make_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    base_strings = [
        b"",  # empty
        b"hello",
        b"warning",
        b"error occurred",
        b"the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog",
        b"/tmp/recast/log.txt",
        b"C:/windows/path\\file.txt",
        b"line1\nline2\nline3",
        b"tabs\tand\tspaces",
        b"percent%%embedded%%signs",
        b"unicode: \xe2\x98\x83 snowman",  # UTF-8 bytes
        b"json:{\"k\":123,\"s\":\"v\"}",
        b"[progress] building compact heightfield",
        b"[warning] area too small, merging",
        b"[error] out of memory while allocating",
    ]
    # Add some random ASCII strings of varying length
    def rand_ascii(n: int) -> bytes:
        alphabet = b"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789 _-.,:/\\"
        return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

    for ln in [1, 5, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]:
        base_strings.append(rand_ascii(ln))

    # Ensure each is null-terminated and without internal nulls (keep as-is)

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_u32(r: random.Random) -> int:
    # Mix edge cases and random values

    if r.random() < 0.4:

    return r.choice(choices)

    # Compose from multiple alphabets and include NULs

    # ASCII words
    words = [b"hello", b"recast", b"detour", b"navmesh", b"tile", b"query"]
    if L > 0 and r.random() < 0.5:
        chunks.append(r.choice(words))

    if r.random() < 0.4:
        fmt = r.choice([b"%s", b"%d", b"%x", b"%%", b"%08x", b"%f"])

        if p < 0.1:
            return 0
        elif p < 0.3:
            return r.choice([10, 13, 9])
        elif p < 0.6:
            return r.randint(32, 126)
        elif p < 0.9:
            return r.randint(128, 255)
        else:
            return r.choice([0, 0, 0])

        b"A" * 128,

MAGIC = b"DDTM\x01"  # simple marker

    return [rng.uniform(-12.8, 12.8) for _ in range(3)]

    # Map [-12.8, 12.8] to [0,255]
    t = (f + 12.8) / 25.6
    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, t))
    return int(round(t * 255))

    # Generate a sequence from quantized positions so repetition still yields coherent spans.
    data = bytearray()
    for _ in range(nverts):
        x,y,z = _rand_vec3(rng)
        data.append(_quantize_float_to_byte(x))
        data.append(_quantize_float_to_byte(y))
        data.append(_quantize_float_to_byte(z))
    # Ensure non-empty
    if not data:
        data.extend(b"\x80\x80\x80")
    return bytes(data)

def _build_ascii_blob_for_indices(rng, nverts: int, ntris: int) -> bytes:
    # Indices are byte % nverts. We want coverage across vertex range.
    # Create bytes that step across range and include boundaries.
    data = bytearray()
    if nverts <= 1:
        # Any value will map to 0
        data.extend(b"\x00\x01\x7F\xFF")
    else:
        # Include 0, 1, nverts-1, values > nverts to test modulo behavior
        base = [0, 1, max(0, nverts-1), nverts, nverts+1, 127, 255]

        while len(data) < needed:
            for v in base:

                if len(data) >= needed:

def _build_ascii_blob_for_flags(rng, ntris: int) -> bytes:
    # Provide varied flag bytes.
    data = bytearray()
    pattern = [0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0x7F, 0x80, 0xFE, 0xFF]
    needed = max(ntris, 8)
    while len(data) < needed:
        # Mix deterministic pattern with random
        for v in pattern:
            data.append(v)
            if len(data) >= needed:
                break
        if len(data) < needed:
            data.append(rng.randrange(0, 256))
    return bytes(data)

def _choose_sizes(rng):
    # Sizes in 0..128 as per stub. Prefer non-zero but occasionally zero to exercise edge cases.
    def pick():
        roll = rng.random()
        if roll < 0.15:
            return 0
        elif roll < 0.85:
            return rng.randrange(1, 33)  # small typical meshes
        else:
            return rng.randrange(33, 129) # larger but bounded
    nverts = pick()
    ntris = pick()
    # If nverts == 0, ensure ntris == 0 to avoid early bail in stub and still exercise path
    if nverts == 0:
        ntris = 0
    return nverts, ntris

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:

    # Decide mesh sizes and option toggles
    nverts, ntris = _choose_sizes(rng)

    # Build ASCII blobs used for different FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in stubs.
    vblob = _build_ascii_blob_for_verts(rng, max(nverts, 1))
    tblob = _build_ascii_blob_for_indices(rng, nverts, ntris)
    fblob = _build_ascii_blob_for_flags(rng, ntris)

    # Compose header values to influence FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) reads:
    # r0, r1 decide nverts/ntris modulo 129; we mirror our choices to maximize chance of match.
    # r2 toggles normals/flags bits in duDebugDrawTriMesh (bit0 normals, bit1 flags)
    use_normals = 1 if rng.random() < 0.7 else 0
    use_flags = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
    r2 = (use_normals & 1) | ((use_flags & 1) << 1)

    # Additional unsigned ints consumed for texScale and slope angle. Provide varied values.
    tex_u = rng.randrange(1, 1000)
    slope_u = rng.randrange(0, 91)
    tex2_u = rng.randrange(1, 1000)

    # To steer modulo in stub close to our chosen sizes, set r0,r1 accordingly.
    r0 = nverts  # modulo 129 yields nverts
    r1 = ntris   # modulo 129 yields ntris

    # Layout the final buffer as:
    # MAGIC
    # u32 count_fields
    # sequence of u32 fields used by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) in likely order across both stubs
    # then distinct sections with tags for FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumption
    fields = [r0, r1, r2, tex_u,  # for duDebugDrawTriMesh
              r0, r1,             # sizes again for second stub if needed
              (use_normals & 1),  # normals toggle for slope
              slope_u, tex2_u]

    header = bytearray()
    header += MAGIC
    header += _pack_u32(len(fields))
    for v in fields:
        header += _pack_u32(v)

    # Add tagged string sections so each FUZZ_PARAM_STR call can read a chunk with variability.
    # We separate with simple tags and lengths so the fuzzer harness reading as a stream still
    # gets plenty of bytes; order: verts, tris, flags, verts2, tris2, flags2
    def chunk(tag: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        return tag + _pack_u32(len(payload)) + payload

    body = bytearray()
    body += chunk(b"VB", vblob)
    body += chunk(b"TB", tblob)
    body += chunk(b"FB", fblob)
    # Add some alternate blobs to diversify subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads
    # Slightly shuffled/rotated versions
    v2 = (vblob[1:] + vblob[:1]) if len(vblob) > 1 else vblob
    t2 = (tblob[2:] + tblob[:2]) if len(tblob) > 2 else tblob
    f2 = bytes(reversed(fblob)) if len(fblob) > 0 else fblob
    body += chunk(b"V2", v2)
    body += chunk(b"T2", t2)
    body += chunk(b"F2", f2)

    blob = bytes(header + body)
    # Guard size
    return blob[:4096]

# optional normals/flags, and reasonable scalar values so that the drawing helpers receive

#
# Layout (little-endian):
#   U32 r0  -> nverts seed (stub uses r0 % 129)
#   U32 r1  -> ntris  seed (stub uses r1 % 129)
#   U32 r2  -> options (bit0 normals, bit1 flags) for first stub
#   U32 r3  -> texScale seed for first stub (0..999 mapped inside)
#   U32 r4  -> normals option for slope stub (bit0)
#   U32 r5  -> walkableSlopeAngle seed (0..90)
#   U32 r6  -> texScale seed for slope stub
# Followed by three blobs used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls in order:
#   vblob  -> vertex coordinate source bytes
#   tblob  -> triangle index source bytes
#   fblob  -> flags source bytes
# Each blob is length-prefixed with U32, then raw bytes.
#
# The stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times. Typically each call consumes the next
# available string from the input. We therefore provide blobs sized to cover their needs.
#
# Vertex fill: verts[i] = ((byte-128)*scale). Index fill: tris[i] = byte % nverts (when nverts>0).
# We choose counts and create blobs large enough: vblob >= 3*nverts, tblob >= 3*ntris, fblob >= ntris.

def _make_mesh(seed: int) -> Tuple[int, int, bytes, bytes, bytes, int, int, int, int, int, int, int]:

    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 127, 128]

        nverts = rnd.choice(choices)

    if nverts < 3:
        ntris = 0
    else:
        if rnd.random() < 0.75:

        else:
            ntris = rnd.choice([0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60])

    use_flags_0 = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.5 else 0
    r2 = (use_normals_0 & 1) | ((use_flags_0 & 1) << 1)

    # Slope stub normals option
    use_normals_1 = 1 if rnd.random() < 0.7 else 0

    # Seeds for tex scales and slope angle
    r3 = rnd.randint(0, 999)
    r5 = rnd.randint(0, 90)
    r6 = rnd.randint(0, 999)

    # Create blobs sized to cover consumption patterns.
    vlen = max(1, 3 * nverts)
    tlen = max(1, 3 * ntris)
    flen = max(1, ntris)

    # Vertex blob: patterned distribution with some structure.
    vblob = bytearray(vlen)
    for i in range(vlen):
        # Mix low/high bytes to get varied coordinates but keep them in 0..255
        base = (i * 37 + rnd.randrange(256)) & 0xff
        # Introduce some planar and vertical structure
        if i % 9 == 0:

        vblob[i] = base

    # Triangle indices blob: ensure coverage of [0, nverts)
    tblob = bytearray(tlen)
    for i in range(tlen):
        if nverts > 0:
            tblob[i] = rnd.randrange(nverts) & 0xff
        else:
            tblob[i] = 0

    # Flags blob: random bytes
    fblob = bytearray(flen)
    for i in range(flen):
        fblob[i] = rnd.randrange(256)

    # r0 and r1 are used modulo 129 to get counts. Encode them so the modulo produces our intended counts.
    # Find values r0, r1 s.t. r % 129 == target.
    r0 = nverts % 129
    r1 = ntris % 129

    # r4 encodes normals flag for slope stub in bit0
    r4 = use_normals_1 & 1

    return nverts, ntris, bytes(vblob), bytes(tblob), bytes(fblob), r0, r1, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:

    nverts, ntris, vblob, tblob, fblob, r0, r1, r2, r3, r4, r5, r6 = _make_mesh(seed ^ 0x9e3779b9)

    parts.append(_pack_u32(r0))  # nverts seed
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r1))  # ntris seed
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r2))  # options (normals/flags) for first stub
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r3))  # texScale seed
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r4))  # normals option for slope stub
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r5))  # walkableSlopeAngle seed
    parts.append(_pack_u32(r6))  # texScale seed for slope stub

    # vblob
    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(vblob)))
    parts.append(vblob)
    # tblob
    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(tblob)))
    parts.append(tblob)
    # fblob
    parts.append(_pack_u32(len(fblob)))
    parts.append(fblob)

    buf = b''.join(parts)

    # Ensure size <= 4096 (per requirement). If larger due to extreme counts, trim blobs conservatively.
    if len(buf) > 4096:

        overflow = len(buf) - 4096

        t = bytearray(tblob)
        f = bytearray(fblob)
        def trim(b: bytearray, need: int) -> int:
            if need <= 0:
                return 0
            cut = min(len(b) // 4, need)  # trim in moderate chunks
            if cut > 0:
                del b[-cut:]
            return need - cut
        overflow = trim(f, overflow)
        overflow = trim(t, overflow)
        overflow = trim(v, overflow)
        # Rebuild with new lengths
        parts = []
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r0))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r1))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r2))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r3))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r4))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r5))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(r6))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(len(v)))
        parts.append(bytes(v))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(len(t)))
        parts.append(bytes(t))
        parts.append(_pack_u32(len(f)))
        parts.append(bytes(f))
        buf = b''.join(parts)
        # Final guard
        buf = buf[:4096]

    return buf

# - Flags (bytes)

# interpreted as integers and as strings (bytes).

    if alphabet is None:

    return bytes(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))

    data = bytearray()

    blob += index_blob2
    blob += tail_ascii

    return bytes(blob[:MAX_TOTAL])

#  - vertex blob (arbitrary bytes, length >= vcount)
#  - triangle indices blob (arbitrary bytes, length >= icount)

# FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME calls in sequence. We craft a self-describing, repeatable byte stream
